# Core

This section contains the authoritative reference documentation for the core components of the system. It is intended for developers who need a detailed understanding of the available APIs, internal architecture, and extension points.

The documentation is organized by functional areas, including managers, utilities, GUI infrastructure, widgets, models, and other foundational modules. Each page focuses on concrete interfaces, responsibilities, and usage patterns rather than high-level concepts or tutorials.

Use this section when you need precise information about classes, functions, data structures, and their interactions, or when implementing integrations, plugins, or advanced customizations.

For task-oriented guidance and complete patterns, begin with [Building plugins](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/index.html) or [Parallel execution](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/parallel_execution/index.html), then return here for exact signatures. API pages link back to the relevant practical guide where one exists.

# AbstractErrorLogger

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_error_logger.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/managers/abstract_error_logger.html`

---

# AbstractErrorLogger

**Qualified name:** `mv::AbstractErrorLogger`

`AbstractErrorLogger` is the application-side base class for an optional error-reporting backend. It receives eligible handled exceptions and user feedback from [AbstractErrorManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_error_manager.html), and it follows the global opt-in and enablement settings exposed by that manager.

This is an application integration point, not the routine logging API for plugins. Plugin code should use Qt logging for diagnostic evidence and report user-visible failures at the boundary that owns the operation. See [Notifications, logging, errors, and diagnostics](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/diagnostics/index.html) for that decision model.

Concrete backends implement initialization, startup, shutdown, and DSN validation. Initialization is deliberately divided into `beginInitialization()` and `endInitialization()` so the base class can connect shared settings and track readiness around backend-specific setup.

class AbstractErrorLogger : public QObject
:   Abstract error logger class.

# AbstractErrorManager

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_error_manager.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/managers/abstract_error_manager.html`

---

# AbstractErrorManager

```cpp
// The core and its managers are located in this header
#include "CoreInterface.h"

// Use this global function to access the errors manager
mv::errors().getDebugStackTrace();
```

The error manager supplies application-level stack capture, consent and reporting configuration, handled-exception reporting, and user-feedback submission. An application may connect it to an [AbstractErrorLogger](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_error_logger.html) backend.

This reporting path is distinct from the local [Qt logging pipeline](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/index.html). Plugin failure-handling patterns are covered in [Notifications, logging, errors, and diagnostics](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/diagnostics/index.html).

**Qualified name:** `mv::AbstractErrorManager`

    :   Gets a formatted stack trace for debugging purposes.

        Returns:
        :   A formatted stack trace, or an empty string if unavailable.

# AbstractPluginManager

**Documentation path:** `api/core/managers/abstract_plugin_manager.html`

---

# AbstractPluginManager

Use the plugin manager to create and destroy managed plugin instances. It applies factory creation policy and performs the surrounding initialization and ownership work. See [Requesting plugin instances](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/communication/requesting_plugins.html) and [Plugin creation policy and instance limits](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/index.html).

```cpp
// The core and its managers are located in this header
#include "CoreInterface.h"

// Use this global function to access the plugins manager
mv::plugins().requestPlugin("PluginKind");
```

## Related

- Plugins [models](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugins/index.html)
- [Plugin communication and creation triggers](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/communication/index.html)

# AbstractProjectManager

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_project_manager.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/managers/abstract_project_manager.html`

# AbstractProjectManager

```cpp
// The core and its managers are located in this header
#include "CoreInterface.h"

// Use this global function to access the project manager
mv::projects().saveProject(filePath);
```

## Opening published projects

Published projects open read-only by default. When the standard Open Project dialog detects a published project, it offers **Allow edit of published project**. The choice is represented by `ProjectOpenParameters::allowEditOfPublishedProject` and is applied after opening completes successfully.

Calls that supply a file path directly do not display this dialog and retain the default value, `false`. Treat editable opening as an explicit authoring operation rather than the normal published-project experience. See [Publishing a project](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_applications/publishing_a_project.html) for the user-facing workflow.

## Related

- Project [models](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/projects/index.html)
- [Project serialization and restoration](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/persistence/index.html)

# AbstractSettingsManager

```cpp
// The core and its managers are located in this header
#include "CoreInterface.h"

// Use this global function to access the settings manager reference
mv::settings().getPluginGlobalSettingsGroupAction(...);
```

**Qualified name:** `mv::AbstractSettingsManager`

`AbstractSettingsManager` exposes the application’s built-in settings groups and looks up global settings registered by plugin factories. Plugin-owned groups, defaults, and persistence are described in [Global plugin settings](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/global_settings/index.html).

# Managers

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/managers/index.html`

---

# Managers

Managers are central coordination components in ManiVault. They encapsulate ownership, lifecycle management, and access to related subsystems such as actions, data, projects, and application state.

Rather than exposing raw collections or global services, ManiVault uses manager classes to provide a well-defined interface for querying, modifying, and observing system-wide resources. This helps keep responsibilities clearly separated and enables plugins and applications to interact with the platform in a controlled and consistent manner.

Each manager typically focuses on a specific domain and exposes a stable API for that domain. The following sections document the available manager classes and their public interfaces.

- [AbstractManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_manager.html)
- [AbstractActionsManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_actions_manager.html)
- [AbstractDataHierarchyManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_data_hierarchy_manager.html)
- [AbstractDataManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_data_manager.html)
- [AbstractErrorManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_error_manager.html)
- [AbstractErrorLogger](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_error_logger.html)
- [AbstractEventManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_event_manager.html)
- [AbstractHelpManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_help_manager.html)
- [AbstractPluginManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_plugin_manager.html)
- [AbstractProjectManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_project_manager.html)
- [AbstractScriptingManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_scripting_manager.html)
- [AbstractSettingsManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_settings_manager.html)
- [AbstractTaskManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_task_manager.html)
- [AbstractThemeManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_theme_manager.html)

# Actions

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/actions/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/actions/index.html`

---

# Actions

Actions are re-usable GUI building blocks. During their lifetime, actions are tracked in a global [`mv::AbstractActionsManager`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_actions_manager.html#_CPPv4N2mv22AbstractActionsManagerE "mv::AbstractActionsManager") with the use of dedicated actions models. The classes below are used to store, present and filter actions.

Note

# Color Schemes

Color schemes alter the look-and-feel of **ManiVault Studio**. Color schemes can be added, removed and altered from the GUI. The classes below are used to store, present and filter color schemes.

Note

This API is **stable** and intended for use by **core developers**. Plugin developers typically do not need to interact with it directly, as it is fully wrapped by the [`mv::AbstractThemeManager`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_theme_manager.html#_CPPv4N2mv20AbstractThemeManagerE "mv::AbstractThemeManager").

- [AbstractColorSchemesModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/color_schemes/abstract_color_schemes_model.html)
- [ColorSchemesListModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/color_schemes/color_schemes_list_model.html)
- [ColorSchemesFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/color_schemes/color_schemes_filter_model.html)

# Abstract data hierarchy model

`AbstractDataHierarchyModel` provides the shared roles, columns, item access, and synchronization used by concrete hierarchy models.

class AbstractDataHierarchyModel : public mv::[StandardItemModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/common/standard_item_model.html#_CPPv4N2mv17StandardItemModelE "mv::StandardItemModel")
:   Abstract data hierarchy model class.

    Abstract standard item model class for managing the data hierarchy

    **Author**
    :   Thomas Kroes

    Subclassed by mv::DataHierarchyListModel, [mv::DataHierarchyTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/data_hierarchy/data_hierarchy_tree_model.html#classmv_1_1DataHierarchyTreeModel)

    Public Types

    :   [Dataset](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/data/dataset.html#classmv_1_1Dataset) columns.

        *Values:*

        enumerator Name

        enumerator Location
        :   Name of the dataset.

        enumerator DatasetId
        :   Location of the dataset.

        enumerator RawDataName
        :   Globally unique dataset identifier.

        enumerator RawDataSize
        :   Name of the raw data.

        enumerator SourceDatasetId

        enumerator Progress

        enumerator SelectionGroupIndex

        enumerator IsGroup
        :   Whether the dataset is visible or not.

        enumerator IsDerived
        :   Whether the dataset is composed of other datasets.

        enumerator IsSubset
        :   Whether the dataset is derived from another dataset.

        enumerator IsLocked
        :   Whether the dataset is a subset or not.

        enumerator Count
        :   Whether the dataset is locked.

# Data hierarchy models

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/data_hierarchy/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/data_hierarchy/index.html`

---

# Data hierarchy models

These models present and filter the project data hierarchy for specialized Qt item views. Most plugin code should use `Dataset<T>`, `DataHierarchyItem`, and `mv::dataHierarchy()` directly.

For guidance on when to use a model and how to avoid duplicating hierarchy state, see [Building a custom hierarchy view](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/data/hierarchy/custom_views.html).

- [Abstract data hierarchy model](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/data_hierarchy/abstract_data_hierarchy_model.html)
- [Data hierarchy tree model](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/data_hierarchy/data_hierarchy_tree_model.html)
- [Data hierarchy filter model](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/data_hierarchy/data_hierarchy_filter_model.html)

`ActionsListModel` is an actions model and is documented separately from the hierarchy model family.

# Datasets

Datasets are stored in the [`mv::AbstractDataManager`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_data_manager.html#_CPPv4N2mv19AbstractDataManagerE "mv::AbstractDataManager") and their lifetime is tracked by the model classes below.

Note

This API is **stable** and intended for use by **core developers**. Plugin developers typically do not need to interact with it directly, as it is fully wrapped by the [`mv::AbstractDataManager`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_data_manager.html#_CPPv4N2mv19AbstractDataManagerE "mv::AbstractDataManager").

# Hardware Specs

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/hardware_spec/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/hardware_spec/index.html`

---

# Hardware Specs

A [`mv::util::HardwareSpec`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/hardware_spec/hardware_spec.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util12HardwareSpecE "mv::util::HardwareSpec") is used by **ManiVault** to describe the system requirements of a project, including CPU capabilities, available memory, and disk capacity.

This specification can be extended to define both minimum and recommended hardware requirements. When a project is loaded, ManiVault can evaluate the current system against these requirements and notify the user if the available hardware does not meet the minimum specification, or if it falls below the recommended level.

The model classes below are for storing and filtering hardware specs.

- [AbstractHardwareSpecModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/hardware_spec/abstract_hardware_spec_model.html)
- [HardwareSpecTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/hardware_spec/hardware_spec_tree_model.html)
- [HardwareSpecFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/hardware_spec/hardware_spec_filter_model.html)

# Heads-up-display

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/hud/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/hud/index.html`

---

# Heads-up-display

A **heads-up-display** is used by **ManiVault** to overlay (textual) information on view plugins. The model classes below are for storing and filtering [`mv::util::HeadsUpDisplayItem`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/heads_up_display_item/heads_up_display_item.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util18HeadsUpDisplayItemE "mv::util::HeadsUpDisplayItem").

Note

This API is considered a **WIP**. Plugin developers typically do not need to interact with the models directly as it is wrapped by the [`mv::gui::ViewPluginHeadsUpDisplayAction`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/internal/view_plugin_heads_up_display.html#_CPPv4N2mv3gui30ViewPluginHeadsUpDisplayActionE "mv::gui::ViewPluginHeadsUpDisplayAction"). This action is a member of the [`mv::plugin::ViewPlugin`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/view_plugin.html#_CPPv4N2mv6plugin10ViewPluginE "mv::plugin::ViewPlugin"): `mv::plugin::ViewPlugin::getHeadsUpDisplayAction()`.

- [AbstractHeadsUpDisplayModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/hud/abstract_heads_up_display_model.html)
- [HeadsUpDisplayTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/hud/heads_up_display_tree_model.html)
- [HeadsUpDisplayFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/hud/heads_up_display_filter_model.html)

# Logging

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/logging/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/logging/index.html`

---

# Logging

These models present the structured records captured by the application [Logger](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/logger.html). `LoggingModel` incrementally exposes new records, while `LoggingFilterModel` supplies severity and text filtering plus sorting for user interfaces.

The models do not form the plugin logging entry point. Plugins emit Qt log messages; the global logger captures them and owns the underlying records. See [Core logging](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/index.html) for the complete pipeline.

- [LoggingModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/logging/logging_model.html)
- [LoggingFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/logging/logging_filter_model.html)

# LoggingFilterModel

**Qualified name:** `mv::LoggingFilterModel`

`LoggingFilterModel` is the sorting and filtering layer for a [LoggingModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/logging/logging_model.html). It supports filtering captured messages by text and Qt message type while preserving the structured column semantics needed for sorting.

class LoggingFilterModel : public mv::[SortFilterProxyModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/common/sort_filter_proxy_model.html#_CPPv4N2mv20SortFilterProxyModelE "mv::SortFilterProxyModel")

# LoggingModel

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/logging/logging_model.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/logging/logging_model.html`

---

# LoggingModel

**Qualified name:** `mv::LoggingModel`

`LoggingModel` presents the [structured message records](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/message_record.html) owned by the application logger. It checks for newly captured messages when the event dispatcher wakes and adds model rows without transferring ownership of the underlying records.

Application interfaces may use this model directly or place a [LoggingFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/logging/logging_filter_model.html) in front of it. Plugin code normally emits Qt log messages instead of inserting model rows.

# Plugin Factories

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugin_factories/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/plugin_factories/index.html`

---

# Plugin Factories

Plugin factories are used to create instances of plugins. The core keeps track of which plugin factories are loaded, for which below model classes are used. These models are also used in the **plugin browser**.

Note

This API is **stable** and intended for use by **core developers**. Plugin developers do not need to interact with it directly, as the core tracks its **plugin factories** internally.

- [AbstractPluginFactoriesModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugin_factories/abstract_plugin_factories_model.html)
- [PluginFactoriesTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugin_factories/plugin_factories_tree_model.html)
- [PluginFactoriesListModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugin_factories/plugin_factories_list_model.html)
- [PluginFactoriesFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugin_factories/plugin_factories_filter_model.html)

# Plugins

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugins/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/plugins/index.html`

---

# Plugins

**ManiVault** manages the lifetime of all plugins through the [`mv::AbstractPluginManager`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_plugin_manager.html#_CPPv4N2mv21AbstractPluginManagerE "mv::AbstractPluginManager"). Plugins are tracked in dedicated **list** and **tree** models, which are primarily used by the UI to present plugin state and structure (for example in the plugin browser). The model classes below are for storing and filtering plugins.

Note

This API is **stable** and intended for use by **core developers**. Plugin developers typically do not need to interact with it directly, as it is fully wrapped by the plugins manager.

- [AbstractPluginsModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugins/abstract_plugins_model.html)
- [PluginsTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugins/plugins_tree_model.html)
- [PluginsListModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugins/plugins_list_model.html)
- [PluginsFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/plugins/plugins_filter_model.html)

# Projects

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/projects/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/projects/index.html`

---

# Projects

**ManiVault** manages the lifetime of projects through the [`mv::AbstractProjectManager`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_project_manager.html#_CPPv4N2mv22AbstractProjectManagerE "mv::AbstractProjectManager"). Projects are tracked in dedicated **list** and **tree** models, which are primarily used by the UI. The model classes below are for storing and filtering projects.

Note

This API is **stable** and intended for use by **core developers**. Plugin developers typically do not need to interact with it directly, as it is fully wrapped by the projects manager.

- [AbstractProjectsModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/projects/abstract_projects_model.html)
- [ProjectsTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/projects/projects_tree_model.html)
- [ProjectsListModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/projects/projects_list_model.html)
- [ProjectsFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/projects/projects_filter_model.html)
- [ProjectsModelProject](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/projects/projects_model_project.html)
- [ProjectsModelVisibilityController](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/projects/projects_model_visibility_controller.html)

# Raw data

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/raw_data/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/raw_data/index.html`

---

# Raw data

Raw data is a crucial part of the dataset API. During its lifetime, raw data is tracked by the global [`mv::AbstractDataManager`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_data_manager.html#_CPPv4N2mv19AbstractDataManagerE "mv::AbstractDataManager") with the use of dedicated models. The classes below are used to store, present and filter raw data.

Note

This API is **stable** and intended for use by **core developers**. Plugin developers should not interact with it directly, as it is fully wrapped by the data manager.

- [RawDataModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/raw_data/raw_data_model.html)
- [RawDataFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/raw_data/raw_data_filter_model.html)

# Recent Files

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/recent_files/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/recent_files/index.html`

---

# Recent Files

The classes below are used to store, present, and filter recent files. [`mv::util::RecentFile`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/file/recent_file.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util10RecentFileE "mv::util::RecentFile") records metadata such as when a file was last opened, enabling the construction of curated lists of recently accessed projects. The same mechanism can also be used for other file types.

- [AbstractRecentFilesModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/recent_files/abstract_recent_files_model.html)
- [RecentFilesListModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/recent_files/recent_files_list_model.html)
- [RecentFilesFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/recent_files/recent_files_filter_model.html)

# Scripts

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/scripts/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/scripts/index.html`

---

# Scripts

**ManiVault** provides scripting capabilities to automate workflows and extend functionality. Currently, scripting is supported via **Python**, with the possibility of adding other languages (for example **R**) in the future. The models described below keep track of all available scripts and their organization, while the script manager interfaces with these models to manage and execute scripts.

- [AbstractScriptsModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/scripts/abstract_scripts_model.html)
- [ScriptsListModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/scripts/scripts_list_model.html)
- [ScriptsTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/scripts/scripts_tree_model.html)
- [ScriptsFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/scripts/scripts_filter_model.html)

    **Author**
    :   Thomas Kroes

    Subclassed by [mv::TasksListModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/tasks/tasks_list_model.html#classmv_1_1TasksListModel), [mv::TasksTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/tasks/tasks_tree_model.html#classmv_1_1TasksTreeModel)

    Public Types

    enum class Column
    :   [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task) columns.

        *Values:*

        enumerator Name

        enumerator Enabled
        :   Name of the task.

        enumerator Visible
        :   Whether the task is enabled, disabled tasks are not included in task aggregation.

        enumerator Progress
        :   Whether the task is visible in the user interface.

        enumerator ProgressDescription
        :   [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task) progress.

        enumerator ProgressText
        :   Progress description.

        enumerator Status
        :   Progress text.

        enumerator ProgressMode
        :   Status of the task.

        enumerator ID
        :   Progress mode (manual, subtasks or aggregate)

        enumerator ParentID
        :   Globally unique identifier of the task.

        enumerator Type
        :   Globally unique identifier of the parent task (empty string if not a child task)

        enumerator GuiScopes
        :   [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task) type.

        enumerator MayKill
        :   [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task) GUI scopes.

        enumerator Kill
        :   [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task) may kill boolean.

        enumerator Count
        :   Column for killing a task.

# Tasks

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/tasks/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/models/tasks/index.html`

---

# Tasks

A [`mv::Task`](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#_CPPv4N2mv4TaskE "mv::Task") is used to report the progress of a (lengthy) operation, and its lifetime is tracked by the **core** using the models below.

- [AbstractTasksModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/tasks/abstract_tasks_model.html)
- [TasksTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/tasks/tasks_tree_model.html)
- [TasksListModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/tasks/tasks_list_model.html)
- [TasksFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/tasks/tasks_filter_model.html)

# Parallel execution

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/parallel/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/parallel/index.html`

---

# Parallel execution

The parallel API is ManiVault’s preferred high-level interface for scheduled and concurrent work. `Parallel` runs individual operations, processes or maps collections in parallel, and starts staged execution chains. `ParallelExecutionChain` combines sequential and parallel phases while leaving plan construction and executor integration to the underlying workflow framework.

Start with the [Parallel execution developer guide](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/parallel_execution/index.html) for examples, ownership rules, result handling, and thread-safety guidance. Use the [advanced workflow API](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/index.html) only when these high-level operations do not express the required execution model.

- [Parallel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/parallel/parallel.html)
- [Parallel execution chain](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/parallel/parallel_execution_chain.html)

# DataLoadException

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/data_load_exception.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/plugin/data_load_exception.html`

---

# DataLoadException

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::DataLoadException`

`DataLoadException` represents failure to load a particular file. Its `what()` text combines the file path with the technical reason, allowing the UI boundary that owns the load operation to present or record a useful cause.

Throwing the exception does not itself notify the user. Catch or propagate it through the execution mechanism that owns the loader operation, following the [diagnostics guidance](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/diagnostics/index.html). Avoid duplicating the same failure in a log, notification, and dialog.

struct DataLoadException : public std::exception

# Plugin

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/plugin/index.html`

---

# Plugin

Plugins are the primary extension mechanism in ManiVault. They allow new functionality to be added to the platform without modifying the core application, enabling features such as data loading, analysis, transformation, visualization, and export to be developed and deployed independently.

Each plugin follows a common lifecycle defined by the plugin base class and is instantiated through a plugin factory. Depending on their role, plugins are categorized into specific types that determine how they integrate with the application and interact with data and user workflows.

The sections below describe the core building blocks of the plugin system, the available plugin types, and supporting classes used for metadata and shortcut configuration.

For lifecycle, ownership, input, and implementation guidance, start with [Plugin fundamentals](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/fundamentals/index.html). The pages below are the accompanying API reference.

## Base class and factory

All **ManiVault** plugins are derived from a generic **plugin** base class and are created by a **plugin factory**.

- [Plugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin.html)
- [PluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_factory.html)

## Types

ManiVault plugins are categorized by their primary role within the platform. There are plugins for reading, writing, analyzing, transforming and viewing data. The classes below are all derived from the [plugin base class](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin.html).

Each runtime role has a matching factory specialization. Derive the instance and factory from the same pair, and return the matching instance type from `produce()`. Creation must still be requested through the plugin manager; `produce()` is the factory hook used by that managed path, not a public construction shortcut.

| Role | Instance | Factory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Analysis | [AnalysisPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/analysis_plugin.html) | [AnalysisPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/analysis_plugin_factory.html) |
| Loader | [LoaderPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/loader_plugin.html) | [LoaderPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/loader_plugin_factory.html) |
| Transformation | [TransformationPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/transformation_plugin.html) | [TransformationPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/transformation_plugin_factory.html) |
| View | [ViewPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/view_plugin.html) | [ViewPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/view_plugin_factory.html) |
| Writer | [WriterPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/writer_plugin.html) | [WriterPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/writer_plugin_factory.html) |

The data-role pair, `RawData` and `RawDataFactory`, is documented with the [data API](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/data/index.html) because it defines dataset storage rather than an operation over existing datasets.

- [AnalysisPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/analysis_plugin.html)
- [AnalysisPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/analysis_plugin_factory.html)
- [LoaderPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/loader_plugin.html)
- [LoaderPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/loader_plugin_factory.html)
- [DataLoadException](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/data_load_exception.html)
- [TransformationPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/transformation_plugin.html)
- [TransformationPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/transformation_plugin_factory.html)
- [ViewPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/view_plugin.html)
- [ViewPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/view_plugin_factory.html)
- [WriterPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/writer_plugin.html)
- [WriterPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/writer_plugin_factory.html)

## Miscellaneous

The class below are used to compose a plugin shortcut map and adding plugin metadata.

- [PluginShortcuts](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_shortcuts.html)
- [PluginMetadata](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_metadata.html)

**Documentation path:** `api/core/plugin/loader_plugin.html`

# LoaderPlugin

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::LoaderPlugin`

A loader plugin imports an external source into ManiVault. Implement `loadData()` as the loader’s entry point; `AskForFileName()` is available when the loader uses an interactive file choice and remembers the last directory for that plugin kind.

Pair a loader instance with a [LoaderPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/loader_plugin_factory.html). A loader that cannot parse or read a chosen file may report a [DataLoadException](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/data_load_exception.html) through the appropriate user-facing failure boundary.

class LoaderPlugin : public mv::plugin::[Plugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin.html#_CPPv4N2mv6plugin6PluginE "mv::plugin::Plugin")
:   Public Functions

    virtual void loadData() = 0
    :   Should be implemented by loader plugins to parse their specific data.

        This function will be called when the user clicks on the menu item for this loader. The implementation is free to create file dialogs if desired.

    Protected Functions

    QString AskForFileName(const QString &fileNameFilter) const
    :   Asks the user for the name of a file to load data from.

        Opens a file dialog at the directory of the last loaded file. The path of this directory is stored with the application settings (in the registry, on Windows). `fileNameFilter` could be something like “Text Files (\*.txt)”.

# PluginFactory

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_factory.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/plugin/plugin_factory.html`

---

# PluginFactory

The plugin factory describes and creates instances of one plugin kind. For an implementation skeleton and guidance on factory-owned versus instance-owned state, see [Factory and plugin instance](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/fundamentals/factory_and_instance.html).

Factories also advertise supported data and provide default or dataset-sensitive creation triggers. For the relationship between the broad capability declaration and exact selection rules, see [Creation triggers and inputs](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/fundamentals/triggers_and_inputs.html).

A factory may also own and register one settings group shared by every instance of its plugin kind. See [Global plugin settings](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/global_settings/index.html) for the lifetime and initialization pattern.

Factories can similarly register one plugin-kind status-bar action during startup. See [Status-bar integration](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/status_bar/index.html) for ownership, positioning, and multi-instance behavior.

Factories also define whether standard interfaces may offer a plugin and how many live instances may coexist. See [Plugin creation policy and instance limits](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/index.html) before using the instance counters or maximum directly.

Derive a concrete factory from the specialization matching its instance type. The [plugin API overview](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/index.html) lists the analysis, loader, transformation, view, and writer pairs; data-storage factories are documented with the data API.

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::PluginFactory`

# PluginMetadata

This container holds the user-facing metadata supplied by a plugin factory, including its description, summary, authors and affiliations, copyright, license, and shortcut map. For its relationship to `PluginInfo.json`, Qt metadata, and CMake packaging, see [Metadata and build integration](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/fundamentals/metadata_and_build.html). For about, README, repository, and help integration, see [Help and metadata](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/learning_center/help_and_metadata.html).

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::PluginMetadata`

# TransformationPlugin

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::TransformationPlugin`

A transformation plugin performs a focused transformation over one or more input datasets through `transform()`. The managed creation path assigns its input datasets before initialization.

Pair a transformation instance with a [TransformationPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/transformation_plugin_factory.html). See [Choosing a plugin type](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/fundamentals/choosing_a_type.html) for the boundary between transformations and larger analyses.

# TransformationPluginFactory

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/transformation_plugin_factory.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/plugin/transformation_plugin_factory.html`

---

# TransformationPluginFactory

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::TransformationPluginFactory`

`TransformationPluginFactory` identifies a plugin kind as a transformation and narrows `produce()` to return a [TransformationPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/transformation_plugin.html). Use the inherited [PluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_factory.html) capabilities to declare supported data, construct contextual triggers, and configure creation policy.

Inputs are assigned by the managed plugin request path before instance initialization. `produce()` should only allocate the matching concrete instance; it should not perform the transformation or bypass manager ownership.

class TransformationPluginFactory : public mv::plugin::[PluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_factory.html#_CPPv4N2mv6plugin13PluginFactoryE "mv::plugin::PluginFactory")

    :   Produces an instance of a transformation plugin.

# ViewPlugin

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::ViewPlugin`

A view plugin owns an interactive widget and the actions integrated into its title bar, dock areas, and overlays. It can receive datasets during managed creation and later through `loadData()`.

# ViewPluginFactory

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/view_plugin_factory.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/plugin/view_plugin_factory.html`

---

# ViewPluginFactory

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::ViewPluginFactory`

`ViewPluginFactory` identifies a plugin kind as a view, narrows `produce()` to return a [ViewPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/view_plugin.html), and describes initial workspace placement.

The constructor records whether instances are system views and whether they initially float. System-view factories are limited to one live instance by default. A concrete factory may also choose the preferred dock area; the default is the right dock area. These are factory-level policies shared by every instance of the plugin kind.

Request views through the plugin manager so creation policy, input assignment, workspace placement, initialization, and instance accounting remain intact. See [Plugin creation policy](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/index.html).

class ViewPluginFactory : public mv::plugin::[PluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_factory.html#_CPPv4N2mv6plugin13PluginFactoryE "mv::plugin::PluginFactory")

            - **startFloating** – Whether the view plugin is initially floating rather than docker to other view plugins

    :   Produces the plugin.

# WriterPlugin

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::WriterPlugin`

A writer plugin exports one or more ManiVault datasets through `writeData()`. The managed creation path assigns its ordered input dataset selection before initialization.

Pair a writer instance with a [WriterPluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/writer_plugin_factory.html). The factory advertises broad input support and contextual creation triggers through the common [PluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_factory.html) API.

# WriterPluginFactory

**Qualified name:** `mv::plugin::WriterPluginFactory`

`WriterPluginFactory` identifies a plugin kind as a writer and narrows `produce()` to return a [WriterPlugin](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/writer_plugin.html). Concrete factories use the common [PluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_factory.html) input declarations and dataset-sensitive triggers to offer export operations for valid selections.

The managed request path assigns the selected datasets and initializes the instance. `produce()` should only allocate the matching writer and must not be called directly by plugin code.

class WriterPluginFactory : public mv::plugin::[PluginFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/plugin_factory.html#_CPPv4N2mv6plugin13PluginFactoryE "mv::plugin::PluginFactory")

# Task

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/task/index.html`

---

# Task

Tasks report the progress and state of long-running operations to the user. They do not schedule or execute those operations. For substantial new work, prefer the workflow-backed execution facilities and use a task as their GUI progress projection; manage a task directly when execution is owned elsewhere.

In the current design, tasks focus on progress reporting rather than execution itself. Future versions will extend this concept to optionally manage and run worker logic directly, allowing tasks to encapsulate both execution and reporting.

Tasks are closely integrated with the task models, which manage their lifecycle and visibility within the application.

For guidance on choosing between high-level parallel execution, custom workflows, and direct task management, see [Long-running operations and task progress](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/tasks/index.html).

## Related

- Task [models](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/tasks/index.html)

## Base type

- [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html)

## Types

The task classes below are derived from the [task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html) base class.

- [BackgroundTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/background_task.html)
- [DatasetTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/dataset_task.html)
- [ForegroundTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/foreground_task.html)
- [ModalTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/modal_task.html)
- [ApplicationStartupTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/application_startup_task.html)

## Handlers

Task handlers are responsible for presenting task-related information to the user. For example, they may display progress using a modal dialog, a progress bar in the status bar, or similar UI elements.

- [AbstractTaskHandler](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/handlers/abstract_task_handler.html)
- [BackgroundTaskHandler](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/handlers/background_task_handler.html)

- [ForegroundTaskHandler](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/handlers/foreground_task_handler.html)
- [ModalTaskHandler](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/handlers/modal_task_handler.html)

# Task

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/task/task.html`

---

# Task

**Qualified name:** `mv::Task`

`Task` is the common state and progress model behind all task presentations. It reports an operation but does not execute it. Prefer workflow-backed execution for substantial new work; use a presentation-specific task directly when another component already owns execution. See the [practical execution and task guide](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/tasks/index.html).

Important

`Task::Status` has no failed state. Preserve failures through the operation result, exception, or workflow context, and ensure the task no longer remains running.

class Task : public QObject, public mv::util::[Serializable](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util12SerializableE "mv::util::Serializable")
:   [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task) class.

    Convenience class for managing a task.

    [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task) progress can be determined in three ways (see [Task::setProgressMode()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task_1ab8351a413af1cda8f352379838e8e0a1) and [Task::getProgressMode()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task_1af195311d97d0971c0eb827de0d58daa2)):

    - Setting progress directly setProgress(…)
    - Setting sub tasks items via one of the overloads of Task::setSubTasks() and flagging items as finished with [Task::setSubtaskFinished()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task_1ac1ae2037281bfe874df8d872259249c5), the percentage is then updated automatically
    - Computing the combined progress of child tasks using aggregation (initialize with parent task or use [Task::setParentTask()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task_1afcedf165c947f1e93761a7c9914c5436))

    Tasks have a scope which defines how the content is presented in the user interface (see Task::setScope() and Task::getScope())

    - All background tasks are aggregated into one overarching task and presented in the status bar
    - Foreground tasks automatically show up in a popup at the right of the status bar
    - Modal tasks show up in a modal tasks dialog which blocks all other user interaction

    There is no need to create a user interface to kill tasks, all scopes have controls to kill a task. Connect to the [Task::requestAbort()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task_1a233f014be89ae47fe080327655380da8) signal to be notified when a task was aborted so that further action can be taken.

    Special notes:

    - Tasks should work cross threads (this has only been tested using QThread though)
    - For a more detail exploration of all tasks in the system, a tasks view system plugin is available
    - In case of a tasks hierarchy, all task objects should be in the same QThread context

    **Author**
    :   Thomas Kroes

    Subclassed by [mv::ApplicationStartupTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/application_startup_task.html#classmv_1_1ApplicationStartupTask), [mv::BackgroundTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/background_task.html#classmv_1_1BackgroundTask), [mv::DatasetTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/dataset_task.html#classmv_1_1DatasetTask), [mv::ForegroundTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/foreground_task.html#classmv_1_1ForegroundTask), [mv::ModalTask](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/types/modal_task.html#classmv_1_1ModalTask)

    Public Types

    enum class ConfigurationFlag
    :   Describes the configuration options.

        *Values:*

        enumerator OverrideAggregateStatus

        enumerator Default
        :   Status is not automatically based on child tasks but will be set manually.

    enum class Status
    :   [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task):

        :   …is in the process of being aborted

    Public Functions

# DatasetTask

# Exception presentation helpers

The overloads below show a modal error dialog for a reason, standard exception, or `ManiVaultException`. Use them only at the GUI boundary that consumes the failure.

void mv::util::exceptionMessageBox(const QString &title, const QString &reason, QWidget \*parent = nullptr)
:   Shows a modal exception dialog with a custom reason.

    The dialog displays the supplied reason, includes technical stack-trace details when available from the active error manager, and offers a copy action for the full report.

    Parameters:
    :   - **title** – Dialog title.
        - **reason** – Human-readable explanation of the error.
        - **parent** – Optional parent widget.

void mv::util::exceptionMessageBox(const QString &title, const std::exception &exception, QWidget \*parent = nullptr)
:   Shows a modal exception dialog for a standard C++ exception.

    Parameters:
    :   - **title** – Dialog title.
        - **exception** – Exception whose what() text is shown as the error reason.
        - **parent** – Optional parent widget.

void mv::util::exceptionMessageBox(const QString &title, const [ManiVaultException](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/exception/mani_vault_exception.html#_CPPv4N2mv18ManiVaultExceptionE "mv::ManiVaultException") &exception, QWidget \*parent = nullptr)
:   Shows a modal exception dialog for a ManiVault exception.

    The dialog uses the exception message and stack trace carried by the [ManiVaultException](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/exception/mani_vault_exception.html#classmv_1_1ManiVaultException) instance.

    Parameters:
    :   - **title** – Dialog title.
        - **exception** – ManiVault exception to display.
        - **parent** – Optional parent widget.

# Exceptions

ManiVault provides a structured exception for failures that need severity, separate user-facing and technical text, diagnostic details, source context, and stack metadata. Modal exception helpers are presentation facilities for GUI boundaries.

For practical guidance, see [Exceptions and diagnostic context](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/diagnostics/exceptions.html).

- [ManiVault exception](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/exception/mani_vault_exception.html)
- [Exception presentation helpers](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/exception/exception_helpers.html)

# ManiVault exception

`ManiVaultException` extends `std::runtime_error` with structured application diagnostic context.

class ManiVaultException : public std::runtime\_error
:   Exception type carrying ManiVault diagnostic context.

    [ManiVaultException](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/exception/mani_vault_exception.html#classmv_1_1ManiVaultException) extends std::runtime\_error with severity, user-facing message text, technical cause, source/context location, structured details, a diagnostic identifier, and captured debug stack trace metadata. It is used when errors need to be shown to users and reported with enough context for diagnostics.

    @maintainer Thomas Kroes (BioVault - Biomedical Visual Analytics Unit LUMC - TU Delft)

    Subclassed by [mv::AbstractProjectManager::ProjectDownloadException](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_project_manager.html#classmv_1_1AbstractProjectManager_1_1ProjectDownloadException)

    Public Functions

    ManiVaultException(util::[SeverityLevel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/exception/mani_vault_exception.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util13SeverityLevelE "mv::util::SeverityLevel") severity, QString message, QString what, QString where = {}, QVariantMap details = {}, std::source\_location location = std::source\_location::current())
    :   Constructs a ManiVault exception.

        The constructor stores source-location metadata, creates a diagnostic id, and appends the current debug stack trace to the details map.

        Parameters:
        :   - **severity** – Severity associated with the exception.
            - **message** – User-facing exception message.
            - **what** – Technical cause or short diagnostic description.
            - **where** – Optional source or workflow context where the error occurred.
            - **details** – Optional structured diagnostic details.
            - **location** – C++ source location captured at the throw site.

    [ManiVaultException](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/exception/mani_vault_exception.html#_CPPv4N2mv18ManiVaultExceptionE "mv::ManiVaultException") withAddedDetails(const QVariantMap &additionalDetails) const
    :   Returns a copy of this exception with additional details.

        Additional detail keys overwrite existing keys with the same name.

        Parameters:
        :   **additionalDetails** – Details to merge into the copied exception.

        Returns:
        :   New exception containing the merged details.

    util::[SeverityLevel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/exception/mani_vault_exception.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util13SeverityLevelE "mv::util::SeverityLevel") getSeverity() const
    :   Returns the exception severity.

        Returns:
        :   Severity level.

    QString getMessage() const
    :   Returns the user-facing exception message.

        Returns:
        :   Exception message.

    QString getWhat() const
    :   Returns the technical exception cause.

        Returns:
        :   Technical exception text.

    QString getWhere() const
    :   Returns the source or context where the exception occurred.

        Returns:
        :   Context location string.

    QVariantMap getDetails() const
    :   Returns structured diagnostic details.

        Returns:
        :   Diagnostic details map.

    QUuid getDiagnosticId() const
    :   Returns the unique diagnostic identifier.

        Returns:
        :   Diagnostic id.

    util::StackTrace getStackTrace() const
    :   Returns the captured debug stack trace.

        Returns:
        :   Stack trace frames.

        virtual bool open(QNetworkReply \*reply, const QUrl &url, const QString &targetDirectory, bool overwriteAllowed, QString \*error) = 0
        :   Finalize successfully (e.g., commit QSaveFile)

            Parameters:
            :   - **reply** – Pointer to network reply (may not be nullptr)
                - **url** – Url to download
                - **targetDirectory** – Target directory where to put the download
                - **overwriteAllowed** – Whether it is allowed to overwrite an existing download
                - **error** – Pointer to error

            Returns:
            :   Whether successfully opened

        virtual bool write(const QByteArray &chunk, QString \*error) = 0
        :   Write `chunk` with `error`.

            Parameters:
            :   - **chunk** – Chunk of data
                - **error** – Pointer to error

            Returns:
            :   Whether successfully written

        virtual bool commit(QString \*error) = 0
        :   Finalize successfully (e.g., commit QSaveFile)

            Parameters:
            :   **error** – Pointer to error

            Returns:
            :   Whether commit was successful

        virtual void cancel() noexcept = 0
        :   Discards partial output.

        virtual Result result() const = 0
        :   Get the resulting value to emit into the promise.

            Returns:
            :   The promise result

# Icon

This section documents the classes and helper functions used to create, style, and compose icons within the user interface. It covers icon styling infrastructure as well as utility functions for generating composite icons, overlays, and badge-enhanced variants used throughout the application and its plugins.

# StyledIcon

`StyledIcon` creates theme-aware icons from bundled icon fonts and can apply palette roles, fixed colors, modifiers, and badges. For practical selection and styling patterns, see [Using icons in plugins](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/icons.html).

**Qualified name:** `mv::util::StyledIcon`

class StyledIcon
:   Styled icon class.

    [StyledIcon](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/icon/styled_icon.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1StyledIcon) class is a wrapper around QIcon that allows for easy creation of icons from icon fonts.

    - Support icon fonts (FontAwesome, Material Design Icons, etc.)
    - Supports custom icons
    - Theme-aware (due to [StyledIconEngine](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/icon/styled_icon_engine.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1StyledIconEngine))

    **Author**

            - **iconFontVersion** – [Version](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/internal/version.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Version) of the icon font

    explicit StyledIcon(const QIcon &other)

# Logging

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/util/logging/index.html`

---

# Logging

ManiVault installs a global Qt message handler that turns diagnostic output into structured [MessageRecord](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/message_record.html) entries held by [Logger](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/logger.html). The [logging models](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/logging/index.html) expose those records to application interfaces for display, filtering, and sorting.

Plugin code normally writes through Qt’s `qDebug()`, `qInfo()`, `qWarning()`, and `qCritical()` functions. It should not append records to the global logger or manipulate the presentation models directly. See [Logging diagnostic evidence](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/diagnostics/logging.html) for severity selection, useful context, and privacy guidance.

## Logging and error reporting are different paths

This logger records local diagnostic messages. Optional reporting of handled exceptions or crashes is coordinated by [AbstractErrorManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_error_manager.html) and a consent-aware [AbstractErrorLogger](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_error_logger.html) backend. Writing a Qt log message does not replace user-facing error handling, and it should not be treated as an instruction to send telemetry.

- [MessageRecord](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/message_record.html)
- [Logger](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/logger.html)

# Logger

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/logger.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/util/logging/logger.html`

---

# Logger

**Qualified name:** `mv::util::Logger`

`Logger` is the application-owned store behind ManiVault’s global Qt message handler. It maintains structured [MessageRecord](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/message_record.html) entries, provides synchronized access to them, and supports the models that present newly captured records in the interface.

Application startup initializes the logger. Plugin code should emit Qt log messages rather than construct or initialize another `Logger`. The record-access and mutex APIs primarily support Core presentation and integration code.

class Logger
:   Global application logger.

    Class for recording log messages

    **Author**
    :   Niels Dekker (original design) and Thomas Kroes (re-design and refactor)

    Friends

    *friend class* mv::Application

# MessageRecord

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/message_record.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/util/logging/message_record.html`

---

# MessageRecord

**Qualified name:** `mv::util::MessageRecord`

`MessageRecord` is the structured representation of one captured Qt log message. In addition to the message text and `QtMsgType`, it retains sequence, source-location, function, category, and format-version information for presentation and support diagnostics.

Records are owned by the application [Logger](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/logger.html). Consumers such as `LoggingModel` retain references to those records, so callers should not treat record pointers as independently owned objects.

struct MessageRecord

# Notification

**Qualified name:** `mv::util::Notification`

class Notification : public QWidget
:   Toast-style notification widget.

    [Notification](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/notifications/notification.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Notification) renders one transient message in a stacked notification area. [Notifications](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/notifications/notifications.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Notifications) can either show a title, description, and icon for a fixed or calculated duration, or stay visible while an associated [Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task) is running.

    Instances are linked to previous and next notifications so stacked widgets can reposition when one is shown or dismissed. [Notifications](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/notifications/notifications.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Notifications) owns the lifecycle of these widgets.

    @maintainer Thomas Kroes (BioVault - Biomedical Visual Analytics Unit LUMC - TU Delft)

    Note

    This class is intended for internal use by [Notifications](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/notifications/notifications.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Notifications).

    Public Types

    enum class DurationType
    :   Duration policy for a notification.

        *Values:*

        enumerator Fixed
        :   Uses the standard fixed display duration.

        enumerator Calculated
        :   Estimates display duration from message length.

        enumerator Task
        :   Stays visible while the associated task is running.

    Public Functions

    explicit Notification(const QString &title, const QString &description, const QIcon &icon, [Notification](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/notifications/notification.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util12Notification12NotificationERK7QStringRK7QStringRK5QIconP12NotificationRK12DurationTypeP7QWidget "mv::util::Notification::Notification") \*previousNotification, const [DurationType](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/notifications/notification.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util12Notification12DurationTypeE "mv::util::Notification::DurationType") &durationType, QWidget \*parent = nullptr)
    :   Constructs a message notification.

        Parameters:

            - **icon** – [Notification](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/notifications/notification.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Notification) icon.
            - **previousNotification** – Previous notification in the stack, or nullptr.
            - **durationType** – Display duration policy.
            - **parent** – Optional parent widget.

    explicit Notification(QPointer<[Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#_CPPv4N2mv4TaskE "mv::Task")> task, [Notification](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/notifications/notification.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util12Notification12NotificationE8QPointerI4TaskEP12NotificationP7QWidget "mv::util::Notification::Notification") \*previousNotification, QWidget \*parent = nullptr)

enum class mv::util::PixelSelectionType
:   Pixel selection types enum.

    *Values:*

    enumerator Rectangle

    enumerator Line
    :   Select pixels within a rectangle.

    enumerator Brush
    :   Select pixels within a line.

    enumerator Lasso
    :   A brush is used the paint the pixel selection.

    enumerator Polygon
    :   A lasso tool is used to select pixels.

    enumerator Sample
    :   Select pixels in the interior of a polygon.

    enumerator ROI
    :   Probe one pixel at a time.

        Select all pixels in a ROI

class PixelSelectionTool : public QObject
:   Pixel selection tool class.

    Class for pixel selection using various tools (e.g. brush, rectangle and lasso) It handles mouse/keyboard events to switch between tools and perform the selection itself It draws an overlay of the selection shape `_shapePixmap` and the selected area `_areaPixmap`

# BlobCodec

# BlobCodec

**Qualified name:** `mv::util::BlobCodec`

`BlobCodec` is the abstract binary encoder and decoder used by project blob storage. A codec can encode to memory or a file, decode into a new or existing buffer, declare its file extension, and indicate whether its encoded data may be stored inline.

Codecs are created from settings by the [CodecRegistry](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_registry.html) rather than constructed directly by plugin serialization code. The associated [CodecSettingsAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/miscellaneous/codec_settings_action.html) remains a GUI object; [CodecActionBinding](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_action_binding.html) manages the lifetime boundary when codec work runs on another thread.

class BlobCodec : public QObject
:   Interface for encoding and decoding binary blobs.

    A blob codec transforms raw binary data into a stored representation and back again. Concrete implementations may perform no compression, Qt compression, Zstandard compression, etc.

    **Author**
    :   Thomas Kroes

    Public Types

    enum class Type
    :   Blob codec type.

        *Values:*

        enumerator None

        enumerator QtCompress
        :   No compression.

        enumerator Zstd
        :   Qt compression.

        enumerator Count
        :   Zstandard compression.

    Public Functions

    BlobCodec(QObject \*parent, const gui::CodecSettingsActionPtr &codecSettingsAction)
    :   Constructs a codec with a codec settings action.

        Parameters:
        :   - **parent** – Pointer to parent object
            - **codecSettingsAction** – Codec settings action for this codec (must be a valid pointer)

    virtual [Type](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util9BlobCodec4TypeE "mv::util::BlobCodec::Type") getType() const = 0
    :   Returns the codec type.

    virtual QString getName() const = 0
    :   Returns the codec name used for serialization/debugging.

        This method will throw an exception if encoding fails. The returned QByteArray is only valid if the encoding was successful.

        Parameters:

        :   Encoded bytes

    :   Encode a block of raw bytes and return the encoded data.

        Note

        This method will throw an exception if encoding fails. The returned QByteArray is only valid if the encoding was successful.

        Parameters:

            - **size** – Size of the raw input bytes in bytes

# BlobCodecFactory

# BlobCodecFactory

**Qualified name:** `mv::util::BlobCodecFactory`

A factory describes one codec type, creates its default GUI settings, and creates configured codec instances. Factories are registered with the [CodecRegistry](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_registry.html) by the application integration layer.

Factory objects are expected to live on the main thread because they create [CodecSettingsAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/miscellaneous/codec_settings_action.html) instances. The codecs they produce may subsequently perform encoding or decoding in workflow worker threads.

class BlobCodecFactory : public QObject
:   Factory interface for creating codec instances.

    This factory is expected to live in the main thread

    **Author**
    :   Thomas Kroes

    Public Functions

    :   Get default codec settings action for this codec (returns nullptr if no settings are needed)

        Returns:

    Protected Functions

    virtual std::shared\_ptr<[BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util9BlobCodecE "mv::util::BlobCodec")> createCodec(QObject \*parent, gui::[CodecSettingsAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/miscellaneous/codec_settings_action.html#_CPPv4N2mv3gui19CodecSettingsActionE "mv::gui::CodecSettingsAction") \*codecSettingsAction = nullptr) const = 0
    :   Create a new codec instance with the provided codec settings action.

        If no codec settings action is provided, the default codec settings action is used (if available).

            - **codecSettingsAction** – Codec settings action for the created codec instance (optional)

        Returns:
        :   A new codec instance

# CodecActionBinding

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_action_binding.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/util/serialization/codec_action_binding.html`

---

# CodecActionBinding

**Qualified name:** `mv::util::CodecActionBinding`

`CodecActionBinding` safely associates a [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html) with its [CodecSettingsAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/miscellaneous/codec_settings_action.html). It deliberately avoids making the GUI action a child of a codec that may live or be destroyed on a worker thread. When the codec is destroyed, the action is scheduled for deletion in the GUI thread.

This is primarily an ownership utility for codec implementations and factories; ordinary serializers do not need to create bindings themselves.

class CodecActionBinding : public QObject
:   Binds a [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1BlobCodec) instance to its corresponding GUI CodecSettingsAction.

    [CodecActionBinding](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_action_binding.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1CodecActionBinding) provides a safe bridge between the runtime codec layer and the GUI layer. It ensures that a [gui::CodecSettingsAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/miscellaneous/codec_settings_action.html#classmv_1_1gui_1_1CodecSettingsAction) is properly cleaned up when the associated [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1BlobCodec) is destroyed, without introducing direct ownership or parent-child relationships between objects that may live in different threads.

    This class exists to avoid common pitfalls:

    - Prevents dangling pointers to GUI actions when codecs are destroyed
    - Avoids illegal QObject parenting across threads
    - Decouples GUI lifetime management from codec runtime logic

    The binding listens to the destruction of the [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1BlobCodec) and schedules the deletion of the associated CodecSettingsAction using deleteLater(), ensuring that deletion occurs safely in the GUI thread.

    **Author**
    :   Thomas Kroes

    Public Functions

    CodecActionBinding([BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html#_CPPv4N2mv4util9BlobCodecE "mv::util::BlobCodec") \*codec, gui::[CodecSettingsAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/miscellaneous/codec_settings_action.html#_CPPv4N2mv3gui19CodecSettingsActionE "mv::gui::CodecSettingsAction") \*action)
    :   Constructs a [CodecActionBinding](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_action_binding.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1CodecActionBinding) that binds a [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1BlobCodec) to a CodecSettingsAction.

        Parameters:
        :   - **codec** – The [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1BlobCodec) instance to bind
            - **action** – The CodecSettingsAction instance to bind

# CodecRegistry

**Qualified name:** `mv::util::CodecRegistry`

`CodecRegistry` maps stable codec types and keys to [BlobCodecFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec_factory.html) instances. Project restoration uses this mapping to recreate the codec named in stored blob metadata, while project compression settings use it to enumerate and create available codecs.

Registration belongs to the application/Core integration layer. Plugin persistence code should use the [blob serialization helpers](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serialization.html) and should not depend on a particular registered codec.
