# Serialization

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/util/serialization/index.html`

---

# Serialization

ManiVault persistence has three related layers:

1. **Object state** — a [Serializable](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html) object converts its state to and from a `QVariantMap`.
2. **Binary payloads** — the [serialization helpers](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serialization.html) partition large byte buffers into blocks and represent those blocks in the object’s variant map.
3. **Encoding** — the active project’s [compression settings](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/project/project_compression_action.html) select a codec through the [CodecRegistry](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_registry.html). A [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html) then encodes or decodes each block.

This separation lets a plugin describe *what* must be persisted without taking responsibility for project-archive layout or the concrete compression implementation. On restoration, each blob records the codec needed to decode it; the registry supplies the matching implementation.

Start with [Project serialization and restoration](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/persistence/index.html) for the plugin contract, workflow boundary, identity rules, and compatibility guidance. The pages below provide the exact low-level APIs.

## Which API should I use?

| If you are… | Start with… |
| --- | --- |
| Persisting plugin or model state | [Serializable](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html) and the plugin persistence guide |
| Storing a large binary buffer | [Blob serialization functions](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serialization.html) |
| Configuring project compression | [ProjectCompressionAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/project/project_compression_action.html) and [CodecSettingsAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/miscellaneous/codec_settings_action.html) |
| Integrating another codec into the application | [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html), [BlobCodecFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec_factory.html), and [CodecRegistry](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_registry.html) |

Prefer the workflow forms of serialization and blob processing for long-running operations. They integrate with ManiVault’s workflow execution, progress reporting, and cancellation. The synchronous APIs remain useful for small, bounded state.

## Blob encoding pipeline

The blob helpers obtain the current project’s codec settings, divide the input into blocks, and create codecs through the registry. `BlobStorageLocation` explicitly chooses whether `bytesToBlobVariantMap()` and `bytesToBlobVariantMapWorkflow()` store the encoded blocks as project-archive files or as base64 payloads inside the project JSON. File storage is the default. Decoding recognizes both representations and follows the codec metadata stored with the blob rather than assuming the project’s current selection.

For an end-to-end plugin example and guidance on choosing a storage location, see [Persisting binary data as blob variant maps](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/persistence/binary_blob_data.html).

`CodecActionBinding` is the ownership bridge between a codec and its GUI settings action. It avoids unsafe cross-thread `QObject` parenting when codec work runs outside the GUI thread.

`PropertiesSerializer` is a specialized internal workflow helper for property maps. It is not the general entry point for plugin persistence.

## Reference

- [Serializable](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html)
- [Serialization](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serialization.html)
- [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html)
- [BlobCodecFactory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec_factory.html)
- [CodecRegistry](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_registry.html)
- [CodecActionBinding](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_action_binding.html)

# PropertiesSerializer

**Documentation path:** `api/core/util/serialization/properties_serializer.html`

# PropertiesSerializer

**Qualified name:** `mv::PropertiesSerializer`

`PropertiesSerializer` provides workflow-based conversion for ManiVault property maps. Core uses it while persisting dataset and set properties so that potentially substantial property values participate in the surrounding serialization workflow.

Warning

This is a specialized, temporary Core helper and may be removed in a future release. Do not use it as the general persistence contract for a plugin. Implement [Serializable](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html) and follow the [plugin persistence guide](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/persistence/index.html) instead.

class PropertiesSerializer : public QObject
:   [PropertiesSerializer](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/properties_serializer.html#classmv_1_1PropertiesSerializer) is a utility class that provides static methods for serializing and deserializing (dataset) properties.

    It uses optimized QVariant serialization that is more efficient than the default QVariant serialization, and it includes a format version in the serialized data to ensure compatibility between different versions of the software.

    The toVariantMap method takes a QVariantMap and returns a new QVariantMap that contains the serialized properties, while the fromVariantMap method takes a source QVariantMap and a reference to a destination QVariantMap, and it populates the destination map with the deserialized properties from the source map. If the format version in the source map is not supported, it throws a runtime error.

    **Author**
    :   T. Kroes

    Note

    This class is temporary; it will most likely be removed in the future when a more robust solution for properties serialization is implemented.

    Public Static Functions

    static workflow::UniqueWorkflowPlan fromVariantMapWorkflow(const QVariantMap &propertiesMap, QVariantMap &destinationPropertiesMap, workflow::SharedWorkflowExecutionContext parentContext = nullptr)
    :   Deserializes the given properties map into a workflow plan.

        Parameters:
        :   - **propertiesMap** – The properties map to deserialize.
            - **destinationPropertiesMap** – The map to populate with the deserialized properties.
            - **parentContext** – The parent workflow execution context.

        Returns:
        :   A unique pointer to the workflow plan that performs the deserialization.

    static workflow::UniqueWorkflowPlan toVariantMapWorkflow(const QVariantMap &propertiesMap)
    :   Creates a workflow plan that serializes the given properties map into a QVariantMap using the optimized serialization format.

        Parameters:
        :   **propertiesMap** – The properties map to serialize.

        Returns:
        :   A unique pointer to the workflow plan that performs the serialization.

    :   Format version for the serialized properties.

# Serializable

# Serializable

**Qualified name:** `mv::util::Serializable`

For choosing between synchronous and workflow overrides, see [Synchronous and workflow serialization](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/persistence/synchronous_and_workflow.html).

class Serializable
:   [Serializable](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable) base class.

    [Serializable](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable) provides the serialization contract for persisting and restoring object state.

    Serialization is exposed through two layers:

    - the synchronous contract: [fromVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a3966d0241455cc4550653495368221cf) / [toVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a7c7c63a0099cfdb650247fddc8b1c30e)
    - the workflow contract: [fromVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a87b350d0d2e10960cb9e7d6f3a55e909) / [toVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a4d7fa8d832c61fd3036addc804ad18bf)

    The synchronous functions are intended for simple, immediate serialization work. They must complete all work before returning and must not start background work, execute workflows, or defer state changes.

    The workflow functions are intended for expensive, staged, parallelizable, or progress-reporting serialization work. They only construct workflow plans; they do not execute them. Execution, scheduling, nesting, progress reporting, cancellation, diagnostics, and output collection are the responsibility of the workflow executor and the caller that composes the workflow.

    The default workflow implementations delegate to the synchronous functions, so simple objects only need to override [fromVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a3966d0241455cc4550653495368221cf) and [toVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a7c7c63a0099cfdb650247fddc8b1c30e).

    Framework code that participates in a larger workflow should compose the workflow returned by [fromVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a87b350d0d2e10960cb9e7d6f3a55e909) or [toVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a4d7fa8d832c61fd3036addc804ad18bf), typically as a nested workflow. It should not call helper functions that hide blocking workflow execution.

    Convenience JSON and parent-map helpers are provided for simple synchronous use cases. They are not workflow orchestration APIs.

    Plugin developers should typically:

    - override [fromVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a3966d0241455cc4550653495368221cf) and [toVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a7c7c63a0099cfdb650247fddc8b1c30e) for simple objects
    - override [fromVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a87b350d0d2e10960cb9e7d6f3a55e909) and/or [toVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a4d7fa8d832c61fd3036addc804ad18bf) for expensive, staged, parallelizable, or progress-reporting operations

    In addition to the primary serialization contract, [Serializable](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable) provides helpers for:

    - working with parent QVariantMaps
    - inserting serialized child objects into QVariantMaps
    - reading and writing JSON documents and files
    - object identity management and serialization diagnostics

    Subclassed by [mv::AbstractManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_manager.html#classmv_1_1AbstractManager), [mv::Application](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/application/application.html#classmv_1_1Application), mv::BiMap, mv::CoreApplication, mv::KeyBasedSelectionGroup, [mv::LinkedData](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/data/linked_data.html#classmv_1_1LinkedData), mv::OrderedMap, [mv::Project](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/application/project.html#classmv_1_1Project), [mv::SelectionMap](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/data/selection_map.html#classmv_1_1SelectionMap), [mv::SortFilterProxyModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/common/sort_filter_proxy_model.html#classmv_1_1SortFilterProxyModel), [mv::StandardItemModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/models/common/standard_item_model.html#classmv_1_1StandardItemModel), [mv::Task](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/task/task.html#classmv_1_1Task), [mv::Workspace](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/application/workspace.html#classmv_1_1Workspace), [mv::gui::ColorMapEditor1DNode](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/colormap/color_map_editor_1d_node.html#classmv_1_1gui_1_1ColorMapEditor1DNode), [mv::gui::HierarchyWidget](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/widgets/internal/hierarchy_widget.html#classmv_1_1gui_1_1HierarchyWidget), [mv::gui::WidgetAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/widget_action.html#classmv_1_1gui_1_1WidgetAction), [mv::util::Version](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/internal/version.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Version)

        In most cases, [makeUnique()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a3bb166d5843f4ef17791915334cc5353) should be preferred when a new identity is required.

    QString getSerializationName() const
    :   Get this object’s serialization name.

        The serialization name is used as the key under which the object is stored in parent variant maps and JSON documents.

        Returns:
        :   Serialization name.

    void setSerializationName(const QString &serializationName)
    :   Set this object’s serialization name.

        The serialization name is used as the key under which the object is stored in parent variant maps and JSON documents.

        Changing the serialization name after serialized data has already been persisted may render that data unreadable by this object, because the expected serialization key no longer matches the key stored in the serialized representation.

        Changing the serialization name may also introduce collisions with other serialized objects or make existing serialized state unreachable.

        Use this function sparingly and only when the object’s serialization identity is intentionally being changed and the implications are fully understood.

        Parameters:
        :   **serializationName** – Serialization name to assign.

    virtual void fromVariantMap(const QVariantMap &variantMap)
    :   Load the object state from a variant map.

        This is the low-level synchronous loading implementation.

        When this function returns, all state represented by the variant map must have been fully applied to the object.

        Implementations must not:

        - start background work
        - schedule workflow jobs
        - return before restoration is complete

        Framework code that participates in workflow execution should generally compose the workflow returned by [fromVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a87b350d0d2e10960cb9e7d6f3a55e909) instead of calling this function directly.

        Override this function for simple objects whose state can be restored synchronously.

        Override [fromVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a87b350d0d2e10960cb9e7d6f3a55e909) instead when loading is expensive, staged, parallelizable, or requires progress reporting.

        Parameters:
        :   **variantMap** – Serialized object state.

    virtual workflow::UniqueWorkflowPlan fromVariantMapWorkflow(QVariantMap variantMap)
    :   Create a workflow that restores the object state.

        This function constructs a workflow but does not execute it.

        The returned workflow must fully restore the object when executed.

        Implementations may use sequential, parallel, nested, or batched stages and may publish progress, warnings, messages, and outputs.

        The default implementation creates a simple workflow that invokes [fromVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a3966d0241455cc4550653495368221cf).

        Framework code may compose this workflow directly, for example as a nested workflow within a larger serialization workflow.

        Parameters:
        :   **variantMap** – Serialized object state.

        Returns:
        :   Workflow plan that restores the object state.

    virtual void fromParentVariantMap(const QVariantMap &parentVariantMap, bool ignoreLoadingErrors = false)
    :   Restore this object from a parent variant map.

        This convenience function looks up the child variant map associated with this object’s serialization name and forwards it to [fromVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a3966d0241455cc4550653495368221cf).

        The function expects the parent variant map to contain an entry whose key matches [getSerializationName()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1ae0ff3065f78d2a8d406c703bd664f61a). The associated value must be a QVariantMap representing the serialized state of this object.

        This function uses the synchronous serialization contract and therefore invokes [fromVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a3966d0241455cc4550653495368221cf) directly. It does not execute [fromVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a87b350d0d2e10960cb9e7d6f3a55e909) and does not participate in workflow execution, progress reporting, or parent workflow hierarchies.

        Use [fromVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a87b350d0d2e10960cb9e7d6f3a55e909) when deserialization needs to participate in a larger workflow hierarchy.

        Parameters:
        :   - **parentVariantMap** – Parent variant map containing serialized child objects.
            - **ignoreLoadingErrors** – Whether missing serialized data should be ignored. When false, missing entries result in an exception. When true, missing entries may be handled according to the application’s loading error policy.

        Throws:
        :   - std::runtime\_error – If the serialization name is empty.
            - [ManiVaultException](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/exception/mani_vault_exception.html#_CPPv4N2mv18ManiVaultExceptionE "mv::ManiVaultException") – If the required entry is not present.

    virtual void fromJsonDocument(const QJsonDocument &jsonDocument)
    :   Restore the object state from a JSON document.

        This function extracts the variant map associated with this object’s serialization name from the JSON document and forwards it directly to [fromVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a3966d0241455cc4550653495368221cf).

        This function uses the synchronous serialization contract and does not execute [fromVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a87b350d0d2e10960cb9e7d6f3a55e909). As a result, custom workflow-based loading behavior, progress reporting, nested workflows, and parent workflow hierarchies are not used.

        Parameters:

    virtual void fromJsonFile(const QString &filePath = "")
    :   Restore the object state from a JSON file.

        This function reads a JSON document from disk, validates that the file exists, can be opened, contains data, and contains a valid JSON document, then forwards the document to [fromJsonDocument()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a74d4ecb28946450b9b85c27c22cb63f7).

        This function performs synchronous file loading and delegates to [fromJsonDocument()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a74d4ecb28946450b9b85c27c22cb63f7) after validating and parsing the JSON document.

        Parameters:

            - std::exception – Any exception propagated by [fromJsonDocument()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a74d4ecb28946450b9b85c27c22cb63f7).

    virtual QVariantMap toVariantMap() const
    :   Serialize the object state to a variant map.

        This is the low-level synchronous serialization implementation.

        The returned variant map must contain all information required to restore the object through [fromVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a3966d0241455cc4550653495368221cf).

        The base implementation serializes only the object’s unique identifier and updates the serialization counter.

        Derived classes should extend the returned variant map with their own serialized state and should generally invoke the base implementation first.

        Implementations must not schedule asynchronous work, create workflows, or defer serialization beyond the lifetime of this call.

        Framework code that participates in workflow execution should generally compose the workflow returned by [toVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a4d7fa8d832c61fd3036addc804ad18bf) instead of calling this function directly.

        The default implementation of [toVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a4d7fa8d832c61fd3036addc804ad18bf) delegates to this function, allowing simple objects to participate in the workflow-based serialization contract without implementing a custom workflow.

        Returns:
        :   Complete variant map representation of the object state.

    virtual workflow::UniqueWorkflowPlan toVariantMapWorkflow() const
    :   Create a workflow that serializes the object state to a variant map.

        This is the workflow-based serialization hook.

        The function only constructs and returns a workflow plan. It does not execute the workflow.

        The returned workflow must publish the serialized QVariantMap as an output using this object’s serialization name.

        The base implementation creates a simple workflow that invokes [toVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a7c7c63a0099cfdb650247fddc8b1c30e) and publishes the resulting variant map as an output.

        Derived classes may override this function when serialization is expensive, staged, parallelizable, or requires progress reporting.

        Implementations must not perform the serialization immediately unless that work is part of a job in the returned workflow.

        Framework code may compose this workflow directly, for example as a nested workflow within a larger serialization workflow.

        Returns:
        :   Workflow plan that serializes the object state when executed.

    void insertIntoVariantMap(QVariantMap &variantMap) const
    :   Insert this object’s serialized state into a parent variant map.

        This convenience function serializes the object using [toVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a7c7c63a0099cfdb650247fddc8b1c30e) and stores the resulting child variant map under the object’s serialization name.

        The function requires:

        - a non-empty serialization name
        - that the parent variant map does not already contain an entry with that name

        This function uses the synchronous serialization contract and therefore invokes [toVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a7c7c63a0099cfdb650247fddc8b1c30e) directly. It does not participate in workflow execution and does not invoke [toVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a4d7fa8d832c61fd3036addc804ad18bf).

        Use [toVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a4d7fa8d832c61fd3036addc804ad18bf) when serialization needs to participate in a larger workflow hierarchy.

        Example:

        ```
        QVariantMap parentMap;
        child.insertIntoVariantMap(parentMap);
        ```

        Result:

        ```
        {
            "ChildSerializationName" : { ... }
        }
        ```

        Parameters:
        :   **variantMap** – Parent variant map into which the serialized object state will be inserted.

        Throws:
        :   - std::runtime\_error – If the serialization name is empty.
            - std::runtime\_error – If the parent variant map already contains an entry with the same serialization name.

    virtual QJsonDocument toJsonDocument() const
    :   Serialize the object state to a JSON document.

        This convenience function serializes the object using the synchronous serialization contract and converts the resulting QVariantMap to a JSON document.

        This function invokes [toVariantMap()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a7c7c63a0099cfdb650247fddc8b1c30e) directly. It does not participate in workflow execution and does not invoke [toVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a4d7fa8d832c61fd3036addc804ad18bf).

        Use [toVariantMapWorkflow()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serializable.html#classmv_1_1util_1_1Serializable_1a4d7fa8d832c61fd3036addc804ad18bf) when serialization needs to participate in a larger workflow hierarchy.

        Returns:
        :   JSON document containing the serialized object state.

# Serialization

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/serialization.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/util/serialization/serialization.html`

---

# Serialization

This section documents utility functions for encoding byte buffers as project blobs, restoring those buffers, and serializing Qt variant maps. Large encode and decode operations can be expressed as workflow plans so that they use the core workflow execution, progress, and cancellation infrastructure.

Blob encoding uses the active project’s [compression configuration](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/project/project_compression_action.html) and creates the selected [BlobCodec](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/blob_codec.html) through the [CodecRegistry](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/serialization/codec_registry.html). Use these helpers instead of coupling plugin serialization directly to a concrete compression library or archive layout.

The encode helpers require an open project because the project supplies the codec settings and persistence context. A serialized blob carries the codec information required for restoration.

## Storage location

`BlobStorageLocation` controls where each encoded block is stored:

- `FileInProject` writes block files into the project archive and stores relative references in the blob map. It is the default and is normally the better choice for large payloads.
- `InlineInProjectJson` stores the encoded bytes as base64 data directly in the project JSON. It produces a self-contained variant-map representation, at the cost of a larger JSON document and base64 overhead.

Both forms use the active project’s codec and block-size settings. The restore helpers accept either representation without a separate storage-location argument. Treat the returned blob map as opaque rather than depending on its internal block fields.

For plugin-oriented examples, see [Persisting binary data as blob variant maps](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/persistence/binary_blob_data.html).

enum class mv::util::BlobStorageLocation
:   Location used to store encoded blob payloads during project serialization.

    *Values:*

    enumerator FileInProject

    enumerator InlineInProjectJson
    :   Store each encoded block as a file in the project archive.

        Store each encoded block inline in the project JSON.

# Context

Context types connect jobs to operation-specific data and framework runtime state. Execution contexts form a hierarchy and share root state, while context payloads carry inputs and intermediate values for a particular operation.

For ownership and synchronization guidance, see [Execution context and shared state](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/workflows/execution_context.html).

- [Workflow context base](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_context_base.html)
- [Workflow context variant map](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_context_variant_map.html)
- [Workflow execution context](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_execution_context.html)

# Workflow context base

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_context_base.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/workflow/context/workflow_context_base.html`

---

# Workflow context base

The polymorphic base for operation-specific data shared through a workflow.

class WorkflowContextBase
:   Optional workflow-specific context shared by all stages and jobs.

    The context is the intended mechanism for sharing input, output, and intermediate data across a workflow. Implementations should use a typed context class when workflow stages need to communicate.

    Thread safety is the responsibility of the context implementation. For parallel stages, prefer per-job output storage followed by a sequential merge stage, or protect shared mutable state with appropriate locking.

    @maintainer Thomas Kroes (BioVault - Biomedical Visual Analytics Unit LUMC - TU Delft)

    Subclassed by [mv::workflow::WorkflowContextVariantMap](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_context_variant_map.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowContextVariantMap)

    Public Functions

    virtual ~WorkflowContextBase() = default
    :   Destroys the workflow context.

# Workflow context variant map

A general-purpose context payload providing synchronized access to named variant values.

class WorkflowContextVariantMap : public mv::workflow::[WorkflowContextBase](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_context_base.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow19WorkflowContextBaseE "mv::workflow::WorkflowContextBase")
:   Shares QVariantMap data between workflow stages.

    This context provides a thread-safe key/value store that can be used by workflow stages to exchange intermediate data during (serialization or deserialization) workflows.

# Workflow execution context

The node-local runtime interface to shared state, progress, reporting, outputs, and cancellation.

class WorkflowExecutionContext : public std::enable\_shared\_from\_this<[WorkflowExecutionContext](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_execution_context.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow24WorkflowExecutionContextE "mv::workflow::WorkflowExecutionContext")>
:   Runtime context for one workflow execution node.

    [WorkflowExecutionContext](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_execution_context.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowExecutionContext) binds together the report node, progress node, shared execution state, optional task, and hierarchy metadata for a workflow, stage, or job. Contexts form a tree that mirrors the workflow plan during execution.

    @maintainer Thomas Kroes (BioVault - Biomedical Visual Analytics Unit LUMC - TU Delft)

    Public Types

    using ReportNodePtr = [WorkflowReportNode](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_report_node.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow18WorkflowReportNodeE "mv::workflow::WorkflowReportNode")::[SharedWorkflowReportNode](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_report_node.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow18WorkflowReportNode24SharedWorkflowReportNodeE "mv::workflow::WorkflowReportNode::SharedWorkflowReportNode")
    :   Shared report node pointer type used by execution contexts.

    using ProgressNodePtr = [WorkflowProgressNode](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow20WorkflowProgressNodeE "mv::workflow::WorkflowProgressNode")::[Ptr](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow20WorkflowProgressNode3PtrE "mv::workflow::WorkflowProgressNode::Ptr")
    :   Shared progress node pointer type used by execution contexts.

    using StatePtr = [WorkflowExecutionState](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/execution/workflow_execution_state.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow22WorkflowExecutionStateE "mv::workflow::WorkflowExecutionState")::[Ptr](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/execution/workflow_execution_state.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow22WorkflowExecutionState3PtrE "mv::workflow::WorkflowExecutionState::Ptr")
    :   Shared execution state pointer type used by execution contexts.

    using Type = [WorkflowExecutionNodeType](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/utilities/workflow_execution_node_type.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow25WorkflowExecutionNodeTypeE "mv::workflow::WorkflowExecutionNodeType")
    :   Semantic execution node type.

    Public Functions

    :   Creates a workflow child context.

        This function creates a new workflow execution context that inherits execution state, reporting infrastructure, progress tracking infrastructure, and task association from the current context while establishing a new execution hierarchy level for a child workflow.

        The created child context:

        - Shares the same workflow execution state
        - Shares the same task association
        - Extends the execution path hierarchy
        - Creates child report and progress nodes
        - Establishes a unique result scope
        - Receives its own unique execution identifier
        - Is classified as a Workflow execution context

        Parameters:
        :   - **name** – Human-readable name of the child workflow context.
            - **weight** – Relative progress contribution weight of the child workflow.
            - **progressMode** – Progress reporting mode used by the child workflow.

        Returns:
        :   Shared pointer to the newly created workflow execution context.

# Abstract workflow plan executor

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/execution/abstract_workflow_plan_executor.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/workflow/execution/abstract_workflow_plan_executor.html`

---

# Abstract workflow plan executor

The public execution contract for root and nested plans, with blocking and asynchronous entry points.

class AbstractWorkflowPlanExecutor : public QObject
:   Abstract base class for workflow plan executors.

    A workflow plan executor is responsible for executing [WorkflowPlan](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowPlan) instances, managing workflow execution contexts, dispatching jobs to the appropriate execution thread, tracking progress, and producing [WorkflowResult](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/results/workflow_result.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowResult) objects.

    Workflow plans can be executed either as root workflows or as nested child workflows. Root workflows own their execution lifecycle and optionally create tasks, notifications, and progress reporting infrastructure. Child workflows execute within an existing [WorkflowExecutionContext](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_execution_context.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowExecutionContext) and contribute their results to the parent workflow.

    Concrete implementations define the execution strategy, scheduling model, threading behavior, and workflow compilation process.

    @maintainer Thomas Kroes (BioVault - Biomedical Visual Analytics Unit LUMC - TU Delft)

    See also

# Execution

Execution types consume workflow plans, schedule their jobs, maintain root execution state, and expose synchronous or asynchronous completion. Callers should use the abstract executor contract rather than depend on the internal scheduling backend.

For the end-to-end lifecycle, see [Execution model](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/workflows/execution_model.html).

# Workflow

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/workflow/index.html`

---

# Workflow

The workflow API provides ManiVault’s advanced execution framework for structured, observable operations. A workflow plan describes sequential or parallel stages containing jobs; an executor runs that plan using hierarchical contexts, progress and reporting nodes, cooperative cancellation, and configurable threading behavior. Completed executions produce structured results containing status, diagnostics, metrics, and published values.

Most developers should begin with the [parallel API](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/parallel/index.html) and the [Parallel execution](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/parallel_execution/index.html) guide. The pages below are the curated class-level reference for custom workflow plans and deeper framework integration. For architectural guidance, see the [Advanced workflow framework](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/workflows/index.html) guide.

## API areas

# Planning

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/workflow/planning/index.html`

---

# Planning

Planning types describe a workflow before it runs. `WorkflowPlan` owns the stage and job graph, handles identify its entities, and option value types configure cancellation, parallelization, batching, profiling, and reporting at the execution boundary.

For design guidance, see [Defining workflows](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/workflows/defining_workflows.html).

- [Workflow plan](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html)
- [Workflow handle](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_handle.html)
- [Workflow options](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_options.html)
- [Workflow batching options](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_batching_options.html)

# Workflow plan

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html`

---

# Workflow plan

The central planning type containing stages, jobs, lifecycle branches, weights, and scheduling policies.

class WorkflowPlan
:   Describes an executable workflow.

    [WorkflowPlan](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowPlan) is a declarative description consumed by an [AbstractWorkflowPlanExecutor](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/execution/abstract_workflow_plan_executor.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1AbstractWorkflowPlanExecutor). It contains main stages, optional success/failure/finalization stages, shared workflow context, and relative progress weight information. Stages may execute sequentially, in parallel, or in batches, and individual jobs can run normal functions or create nested workflow plans.

    @maintainer Thomas Kroes (BioVault - Biomedical Visual Analytics Unit LUMC - TU Delft)

    Public Types

    enum class ConcurrencyMode
    :   Defines how jobs inside a stage are scheduled.

        *Values:*

        enumerator Sequential
        :   Jobs run one after another.

        enumerator Parallel
        :   Jobs may run concurrently.

    enum class StageExecutionPolicy
    :   Defines the workflow phase in which a stage participates.

        *Values:*

        enumerator Main
        :   Main workflow execution.

        enumerator OnSuccess
        :   Runs after successful main execution.

        enumerator OnFailure
        :   Runs after failed main execution.

        enumerator Finally
        :   Runs after main and success/failure stages.

    enum class JobThreadAffinity
    :   Defines which thread a job should run on.

        *Values:*

        enumerator CurrentWorkerThread
        :   Run on the current worker thread.

        enumerator GuiThread
        :   Dispatch to the GUI thread.

    enum class JobCompletionPolicy
    :   Defines how job completion is determined.

        *Values:*

        enumerator Auto
        :   Completion is inferred by the executor.

        enumerator ManualOrNested
        :   Completion is controlled manually or by nested workflow progress.

    enum class JobProgressMode
    :   Defines how job progress contributes to parent progress.

        *Values:*

        enumerator Automatic
        :   Leaf jobs auto-complete when they have no children.

        enumerator Atomic
        :   Nested workflow progress is treated as one job unit.

        enumerator Nested
        :   Nested workflows contribute fine-grained progress.

    using SharedState = std::shared\_ptr<QVariantMap>
    :   Shared mutable variant-map context used by workflow plans and jobs.

    using JobFunction = std::function<void(const [Job](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow12WorkflowPlan3JobE "mv::workflow::WorkflowPlan::Job")&, const SharedWorkflowExecutionContext&)>
    :   Callable job body.

    using JobFunctions = std::vector<[JobFunction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow12WorkflowPlan11JobFunctionE "mv::workflow::WorkflowPlan::JobFunction")>
    :   Collection of callable job bodies.

    using NestedWorkflowFunction = std::function<UniqueWorkflowPlan(const [Job](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow12WorkflowPlan3JobE "mv::workflow::WorkflowPlan::Job")&, const SharedWorkflowExecutionContext&)>
    :   Function that creates a nested workflow plan for a job.

    using WorkflowBatchSizeFunction = std::function<std::size\_t(const SharedWorkflowExecutionContext&)>
    :   Function that resolves a batched stage size from an execution context.

    using OptionalWorkflowBatchSizeFunction = std::optional<[WorkflowBatchSizeFunction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow12WorkflowPlan25WorkflowBatchSizeFunctionE "mv::workflow::WorkflowPlan::WorkflowBatchSizeFunction")>
    :   Optional batched stage size resolver.

    using Jobs = std::vector<[Job](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow12WorkflowPlan3JobE "mv::workflow::WorkflowPlan::Job")>
    :   Collection of workflow jobs.

    Public Functions

    WorkflowPlan(const QString &title, SharedWorkflowContext context = SharedWorkflowContext())
    :   Constructs a workflow plan.

        Parameters:
        :   - **title** – Human-readable workflow name.
            - **context** – Optional shared workflow context passed to jobs.

    [WorkflowHandle](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_handle.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow14WorkflowHandleE "mv::workflow::WorkflowHandle") addStage([Stage](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/planning/workflow_plan.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow12WorkflowPlan5StageE "mv::workflow::WorkflowPlan::Stage") stage)
    :   Adds a fully constructed stage to the main workflow stage list.

        Parameters:

        Returns:
        :   Handle for the added stage.

# Progress

Progress types represent the execution hierarchy independently of diagnostic reporting. Nodes aggregate weighted child progress and retain terminal state; notifiers and presentation utilities can observe the resulting tree.

For progress and cancellation semantics, see [Progress and cancellation](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/workflows/progress_and_cancellation.html).

- [Workflow progress node](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html)

# Workflow progress node

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html`

# Workflow progress node

A hierarchical progress node with weighted aggregation, status, and snapshot support.

class WorkflowProgressNode : public std::enable\_shared\_from\_this<[WorkflowProgressNode](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow20WorkflowProgressNodeE "mv::workflow::WorkflowProgressNode")>
:   Tracks progress for a workflow execution node.

    [WorkflowProgressNode](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowProgressNode) mirrors the hierarchy created by [WorkflowExecutionContext](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/context/workflow_execution_context.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowExecutionContext). Leaf nodes store explicit progress values, while parent nodes derive their progress from the weighted average of their children. This allows the root node to represent aggregate progress for the entire workflow execution.

    The class is designed for concurrent workflow execution. Public accessors and mutators synchronize access internally, and [createSnapshot()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowProgressNode_1a02bfe06deff5373b82cbf7d48e181205) returns a value tree suitable for dashboards, console formatting, and diagnostics.

    @maintainer Thomas Kroes (BioVault - Biomedical Visual Analytics Unit LUMC - TU Delft)

    Public Types

    enum class Status
    :   Defines the lifecycle state of a progress node.

        *Values:*

        enumerator Pending
        :   Node has been created but has not started.

        enumerator Running
        :   Node is currently executing.

        enumerator Completed
        :   Node finished successfully.

        enumerator Failed
        :   Node finished with an error.

        enumerator Skipped
        :   Node was intentionally skipped.

    using Type = [WorkflowExecutionNodeType](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/utilities/workflow_execution_node_type.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow25WorkflowExecutionNodeTypeE "mv::workflow::WorkflowExecutionNodeType")
    :   Semantic execution node type.

    using Ptr = std::shared\_ptr<[WorkflowProgressNode](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow20WorkflowProgressNodeE "mv::workflow::WorkflowProgressNode")>
    :   Shared pointer type for workflow progress nodes.

    Public Functions

    [Snapshot](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow20WorkflowProgressNode8SnapshotE "mv::workflow::WorkflowProgressNode::Snapshot") createSnapshot() const
    :   Creates a recursive snapshot of this progress subtree.

        Returns:
        :   [Snapshot](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#structmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowProgressNode_1_1Snapshot) containing the current node state and child snapshots.

    explicit WorkflowProgressNode([Type](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow20WorkflowProgressNode4TypeE "mv::workflow::WorkflowProgressNode::Type") type, QString name, [Ptr](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow20WorkflowProgressNode3PtrE "mv::workflow::WorkflowProgressNode::Ptr") parent, double weight = 1.0)
    :   Constructs a progress node.

        Prefer [createRoot()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowProgressNode_1a705c6d77026000cdf77726063e922bad) and [createChild()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/progress/workflow_progress_node.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowProgressNode_1aadab8afa20ce66773f0a6387e2167329) in workflow code so parent-child relationships are established consistently.

        Parameters:
        :   - **type** – Semantic workflow node type.
            - **name** – Human-readable node name.
            - **parent** – Parent progress node, or nullptr for a root node.
            - **weight** – Relative contribution to the parent node’s progress.

# AbstractWorkflowMessagesModel

# AbstractWorkflowMessagesModel

**Qualified name:** `mv::AbstractWorkflowMessagesModel`

`AbstractWorkflowMessagesModel` defines the common columns and item behavior used to present [WorkflowMessage](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_message.html) instances. Its columns expose severity, text, emitter, location, details, timestamp, message ID, and parent-context ID.

Each row creates a shared copy of its workflow message, and every item in that row refers to the same copy. The specialized [list](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_messages_list_model.html) and [tree](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_messages_tree_model.html) models decide how rows are organized.

# Reporting and metrics

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/index.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/workflow/reporting/index.html`

---

# Reporting and metrics

Reporting types capture lifecycle events, structured diagnostics, aggregate metrics, and stage summaries. Presentation types render this information for result dialogs and detailed message inspection without owning workflow control flow.

For reporting conventions, see [Reporting, metrics, and profiling](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/workflows/reporting_and_profiling.html).

Workflow messages are part of a particular execution result. They are distinct from the process-wide [Qt logging pipeline](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/util/logging/index.html): messages preserve workflow context and can be shown with the result, while Qt logs provide general developer diagnostics.

- [Workflow message](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_message.html)
- [AbstractWorkflowMessagesModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/abstract_workflow_messages_model.html)
- [WorkflowMessagesListModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_messages_list_model.html)
- [WorkflowMessagesTreeModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_messages_tree_model.html)
- [WorkflowMessagesFilterModel](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_messages_filter_model.html)
- [Workflow report node](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_report_node.html)
- [Workflow metric](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_metric.html)
- [Workflow execution metrics](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_execution_metrics.html)
- [Workflow stage summary](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_stage_summary.html)
- [Workflow result details options](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_result_details_options.html)
- [Workflow result dialog](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_result_dialog.html)

# Workflow execution metrics

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_execution_metrics.html

**Documentation path:** `api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_execution_metrics.html`

# Workflow execution metrics

The synchronized accumulator used to update and snapshot metrics during execution.

class WorkflowExecutionMetrics
:   Thread-safe accumulator for workflow execution metrics.

    Metrics are registered by name and then updated atomically during workflow execution. [snapshot()](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_execution_metrics.html#classmv_1_1workflow_1_1WorkflowExecutionMetrics_1ad7341ca0fc8e0d25e9e74839b7a6b76f) returns value objects suitable for reporting and notifications.

    @maintainer Thomas Kroes (BioVault - Biomedical Visual Analytics Unit LUMC - TU Delft)

    Public Functions

    void registerInteger(const QString &name, const QString &unit, QVariantMap metadata = {})
    :   Registers an integer metric.

        Parameters:
        :   - **name** – Metric name.
            - **unit** – Metric unit label.
            - **metadata** – Additional metric metadata.

    void registerDouble(const QString &name, const QString &unit, QVariantMap metadata = {})
    :   Registers a floating-point metric.

        Parameters:
        :   - **name** – Metric name.
            - **unit** – Metric unit label.
            - **metadata** – Additional metric metadata.

    void addInteger(const QString &name, std::uint64\_t amount)
    :   Adds to an integer metric.

        Parameters:
        :   - **name** – Metric name.
            - **amount** – Amount to add.

    void addDouble(const QString &name, double amount)
    :   Adds to a floating-point metric.

        Parameters:
        :   - **name** – Metric name.
            - **amount** – Amount to add.

    QVector<[WorkflowMetric](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/workflow/reporting/workflow_metric.html#_CPPv4N2mv8workflow14WorkflowMetricE "mv::workflow::WorkflowMetric")> snapshot() const
    :   Returns all registered metrics.

        Returns:
        :   Snapshot of accumulated metric values.

# What actions are

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/actions/what_are_actions.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/actions/what_are_actions.html`

---

# What actions are

An action combines parameter or command state with the ability to create a user-interface representation. Plugins work with the action API; ManiVault supplies the standard Qt widgets and keeps multiple representations synchronized.

Common action families include:

- `StringAction` and `StringsAction` for text;
- `DecimalAction` and `IntegralAction` for numerical values;
- `OptionAction` and `OptionsAction` for choices;
- `ToggleAction` for boolean state;
- `TriggerAction` for commands;
- color and color-map actions;
- file and directory picker actions;
- dataset, plugin, dimension, and dimensions picker actions;
- group and toolbar actions for composition.

An action has a display title, globally unique ID, serialization name, QObject owner, enabled and visible state, widget configuration, and private or public scope. Concrete action types add their own value, range, options, and typed signals.

Use the narrowest concrete type that represents the setting. This provides suitable validation, serialization, signals, parameter compatibility, and standard widgets without custom plumbing.

The [actions API reference](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/index.html) lists the supported concrete types.

# Choosing a communication mechanism

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/communication/choosing_a_mechanism.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/communication/choosing_a_mechanism.html`

---

# Choosing a communication mechanism

Choose the narrowest mechanism that expresses the relationship without making plugins depend unnecessarily on each other’s implementation.

| Need | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Exchange or observe data | `Dataset<T>` handles and dataset events |
| Synchronize compatible parameters | Public and private `WidgetAction` connections |
| Offer a user-invoked command | `TriggerAction` or an attached action |
| Let users create a plugin from selected data | Factory-provided `PluginTriggerAction` |
| Create a known plugin programmatically | `mv::plugins().requestPlugin(...)` |
| Find metadata or contextual triggers without creating | Plugin factory or manager queries |

Prefer dataset and action contracts over casting to a concrete plugin. A direct cast is appropriate only when the caller intentionally depends on that plugin kind and needs an API not represented by a shared abstraction.

Do not cache another plugin’s raw pointer as a general service locator. Plugin instances can be destroyed independently; pass required context during creation or use lifecycle-aware Qt connections.

# Dataset-sensitive plugin triggers

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/communication/dataset_triggers.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/communication/dataset_triggers.html`

---

# Dataset-sensitive plugin triggers

A `PluginTriggerAction` is a discoverable request to create a plugin. Every factory has a default trigger; factories can additionally return contextual triggers for selected datasets or data types.

Override the dataset form when availability depends on actual dataset properties:

```cpp
mv::gui::PluginTriggerActions MyViewFactory::getPluginTriggerActions(
    const mv::Datasets& datasets) const
{
    mv::gui::PluginTriggerActions triggers;

    if (datasets.isEmpty() ||
        !areAllDatasetsOfTheSameType(datasets, PointType))
        return triggers;

    auto* trigger = new mv::gui::PluginTriggerAction(
        nullptr,
        this,
        "My view",
        "Open the selected point datasets",
        icon());

    trigger->setDatasets(datasets);
    trigger->setRequestPluginCallback(
        [this](mv::gui::PluginTriggerAction& action) {
            mv::Datasets validDatasets;
            for (const auto& dataset : action.getDatasets())
                if (dataset.isValid())
                    validDatasets << dataset;

            if (!validDatasets.isEmpty())
                mv::plugins().requestViewPlugin(getKind(), nullptr,
                    mv::gui::DockAreaFlag::Right, validDatasets);
        });

    triggers << trigger;
    return triggers;
}
```

The plugin manager collects, sorts, and initializes contextual triggers before returning them to the UI. `initialize()` assigns the factory icon and stable trigger hash. Code calling a factory override directly must use `PluginFactory::initializePluginTriggerActions()` before presentation.

## Dataset versus data-type overloads

Use `getPluginTriggerActions(const Datasets&)` when count, order, identity, or current state matters. Use the `DataTypes` overload when the operation can be described from types alone. `supportedDataTypes()` is broad factory metadata; it does not replace contextual validation.

Set a task-oriented menu location with `setMenuLocation()` when the default Data, Import, Transform, View, Analyze, or Export path is insufficient. Keep titles concise and tooltips explicit about the selected-data requirements.

# Lifetime and error handling

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/communication/lifetime_and_errors.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/communication/lifetime_and_errors.html`

---

# Lifetime and error handling

Creation triggers often outlive the menu that displays them but contain dataset handles whose implementations can disappear. Validate context at invocation time, not only when constructing the trigger.

## Trigger and callback lifetime

`PluginTriggerActions` stores `QPointer<PluginTriggerAction>`, so consumers can detect deleted actions. A request callback is owned by its trigger. Capture stable values or handles and avoid capturing UI objects without a Qt lifetime guard.

If a callback needs the trigger’s current datasets, read `action.getDatasets()` and remove invalid handles before requesting the plugin. Never retain the callback’s raw plugin result without accounting for plugin destruction.

## Failure boundaries

Programmatic plugin creation can fail because:

- the plugin kind is not loaded;
- the factory cannot produce an instance;
- the maximum instance count has been reached;
- type-specific initialization rejects its inputs;
- plugin initialization throws.

Let expected optionality influence the UI before invocation. At the request boundary, either allow the core’s `ManiVaultException` to reach the standard error handling or catch it where your component can add meaningful context. Do not continue with a null or partially initialized plugin.

## Expensive follow-up work

Keep creation callbacks short. Create and initialize the plugin, then let its normal task or workflow API perform expensive analysis, loading, or transformation with progress and cancellation. A trigger callback runs on the interaction path and should not block the GUI thread.

# Requesting plugin instances

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/communication/requesting_plugins.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/communication/requesting_plugins.html`

---

# Requesting plugin instances

Use the plugin manager rather than calling a factory’s `produce()` directly. The manager checks the kind, enforces instance limits, initializes type-specific inputs, registers the instance, and handles view placement.

```cpp
auto* analysis = mv::plugins().requestPlugin<MyAnalysisPlugin>(
    "MyAnalysisPlugin",
    inputDatasets);

if (!analysis)
    return;
```

The generic request accepts input and output datasets. For analysis plugins the manager assigns both; transformation and writer plugins receive supported input context. A request for a view plugin is delegated to view creation when the project is not currently being restored.

## View placement

Use `requestViewPlugin()` when docking relative to another view matters, or `requestViewPluginFloated()` for a floating view. Pass datasets through the request so initialization follows the normal view-plugin path.

The returned pointer is borrowed from the plugin system. Do not delete it. If it must be retained, use a lifecycle-aware strategy such as `QPointer` and react to QObject destruction.

## Check availability when optional

When integration is optional, call `isPluginLoaded(kind)` or `getPluginFactory(kind)` before presenting the operation. A missing optional plugin should normally remove or disable the integration point rather than fail only after user invocation.

Calling `requestPlugin()` with an unknown kind or after reaching an instance limit fails through the core exception path. See [Lifetime and error handling](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/communication/lifetime_and_errors.html).

# Choosing a creation policy

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/choosing_a_policy.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/creation_policy/choosing_a_policy.html`

---

# Choosing a creation policy

Creation policy has two independent axes:

1. **Discoverability:** should standard ManiVault interfaces offer the plugin?
2. **Multiplicity:** how many live instances may coexist?

Choose both explicitly. Hiding a plugin does not make it a singleton, and limiting it does not hide it before the limit is reached.

## Common policies

| Requirement | Factory policy | Typical example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any number of instances | Keep the default unlimited maximum | Independent views or analyses |
| Exactly one live instance at most | Set the maximum to `1` | Exclusive device or application-wide panel |
| Small finite pool | Set a finite maximum greater than `1` | Expensive GPU-backed views |
| Never user-created through standard UI | Disable standard-GUI creation | Infrastructure created by another plugin or application |
| Valid only for particular datasets | Return contextual trigger actions only for supported selections | Analysis or transformation with exact input requirements |

An instance limit is a **concurrent live-instance limit**. It is not a quota on how many instances may ever be created during the application session. When one instance is destroyed, capacity becomes available again.

## Prefer contextual validity over a global limit

Do not use a maximum to express whether an input selection is valid. Override `supportedDataTypes()` for broad capability discovery and return dataset-sensitive trigger actions for exact constraints such as count, ordering, types, or relationships. The plugin instance should still validate its inputs when it runs.

See [Creation triggers and inputs](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/fundamentals/triggers_and_inputs.html) and [Dataset-sensitive plugin triggers](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/communication/dataset_triggers.html).

## When a singleton is appropriate

A maximum of one is appropriate when two instances would be invalid, rather than merely unusual. Examples include exclusive ownership of hardware, one process-wide coordinator, or a UI whose state is intentionally global.

If multiple instances could be valid but are expensive, first consider whether resources can be shared at factory or service scope. A hard limit changes automation and project compatibility, so it should represent a real product constraint.

## Hiding is not access control

`setAllowPluginCreationFromStandardGui(false)` prevents standard ManiVault surfaces from presenting the factory’s triggers. It does not prohibit creation through the plugin manager, project restoration, scripts, or plugin-specific UI. Treat it as presentation policy, not security or authorization.

# Configuring the factory

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/configuring_the_factory.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/creation_policy/configuring_the_factory.html`

---

# Configuring the factory

Configure stable creation policy on the factory during factory construction or startup, before users can request instances.

```cpp
ExamplePluginFactory::ExamplePluginFactory()
{
    setMaximumNumberOfInstances(1);
    setAllowPluginCreationFromStandardGui(true);
}
```

The setter belongs to `PluginFactory`; there is no instance-level creation policy. Every instance of a kind shares the same factory and therefore the same limit.

## Maximum instances

`setMaximumNumberOfInstances()` sets the number of live instances that may coexist:

```cpp
setMaximumNumberOfInstances(1);  // singleton-like
setMaximumNumberOfInstances(4);  // finite pool
setMaximumNumberOfInstances(0);  // no instance may be created
```

Unlimited creation is the default. The internal value is an unsigned 32-bit integer initialized with `-1`, so code that needs to state the default explicitly can use:

```cpp
setMaximumNumberOfInstances(std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max());
```

Usually it is clearer simply not to call the setter for the unlimited case.

## Standard-GUI creation

Use the standard-GUI flag when instances should only be created by a controlled integration path:

```cpp
setAllowPluginCreationFromStandardGui(false);
```

Standard interfaces such as the data-hierarchy context menu inspect this flag before showing plugin trigger actions. Code may still call `mv::plugins().requestPlugin(...)`, and the normal maximum-instance check still applies.

## Counters are core-owned

Factories expose three related values:

- `getNumberOfInstances()` is the current live count.
- `getNumberOfInstancesProduced()` is the cumulative count produced in this application session.
- `getMaximumNumberOfInstances()` is the concurrent limit.

Do not call `setNumberOfInstances()` or `setNumberOfInstancesProduced()` from plugin code. The plugin manager increments them during managed creation, and plugin destruction updates the live count. Manual changes desynchronize trigger state and enforcement from actual ownership.

The cumulative produced count is useful for diagnostics or unique naming. It is not used to decide whether another instance may be created.

## Keep policy static after startup

Treat the maximum as startup configuration. `setMaximumNumberOfInstances()` changes the stored maximum but does not itself emit a policy-change signal or immediately recompute the standard trigger’s enabled state. The standard trigger is recomputed when the live count changes.

If an application truly needs runtime policy changes, it must explicitly update the surrounding UI and define what happens when the new maximum is below the current live count. Existing instances are not automatically destroyed.

# Plugin creation policy and instance limits

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/index.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/creation_policy/index.html`

---

# Plugin creation policy and instance limits

A plugin factory controls where its plugin can be offered for creation and how many instances may coexist. Configure that policy deliberately when a plugin owns an exclusive resource, has a high resource cost, should only be created in a specific context, or should have one application-wide instance.

Start with [Choosing a creation policy](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/choosing_a_policy.html). Most plugins need only one or two factory settings; the remaining pages explain how those settings interact with triggers, programmatic requests, destruction, and project restoration.

- [Choosing a creation policy](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/choosing_a_policy.html)
- [Configuring the factory](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/configuring_the_factory.html)
- [Triggers and creation requests](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/triggers_and_requests.html)
- [Lifecycle and project restoration](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/lifecycle_and_restoration.html)
- [Testing and pitfalls](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/creation_policy/testing_and_pitfalls.html)

## Core rules

- Put creation policy on the factory, not on a plugin instance.
- Leave the instance limit unlimited unless the plugin has a concrete exclusivity or resource reason.
- Use contextual trigger actions to decide whether a particular dataset selection is valid.
- Request instances through the plugin manager. Never call `produce()` directly.
- Let the core maintain the live and produced instance counters.
- Include project restoration in the compatibility analysis before introducing or reducing a limit.

The relevant API entry points are [PluginFactory and its role-specific factories](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/plugin/index.html), [PluginTriggerAction](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/gui/actions/internal/plugin_trigger_action.html), and [AbstractPluginManager](https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/core/managers/abstract_plugin_manager.html).

# Removal and asynchronous work

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/data/events/removal_and_lifetime.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/data/events/removal_and_lifetime.html`

---

# Removal and asynchronous work

Dataset removal deliberately has two phases. Choose the callback according to what information you need.

## Before removal

`DatasetAboutToBeRemoved` and `Dataset<T>::aboutToBeRemoved()` run before the core destroys the dataset implementation. Use this phase to disconnect dataset-dependent state, remove UI references, or copy small pieces of metadata needed later.

Do not attempt to prevent removal or start new work against the dataset. It has already been marked as about to be removed.

## After removal

`DatasetRemoved` is emitted after the implementation has gone. Its dataset handle is intentionally invalid; `DatasetRemovedEvent` instead supplies `getDatasetGuid()` and `getDataType()`. The handle signal `removed(datasetId)` likewise supplies only the stable ID.

```cpp
if (event->getType() == mv::EventType::DatasetRemoved) {
    const auto* removed = static_cast<mv::DatasetRemovedEvent*>(event);
    forgetDataset(removed->getDatasetGuid(), removed->getDataType());
}
```

## Queued and asynchronous work

A handle that is valid when work is scheduled may be invalid when that work runs. Capture the handle instead of a raw implementation pointer and check it inside the callback:

```cpp
auto points = _points;

schedule([points]() mutable {
    if (!points.isValid())
        return;

    // Access the dataset according to its threading contract.
});
```

Validity only describes lifetime; it does not make the dataset implementation thread-safe. Complete mutations before notifying the event manager so synchronous observers see consistent state.

# Attached actions and context menus

**Source:** https://manivault.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/building_plugins/data/hierarchy/attached_actions.html

**Documentation path:** `development/building_plugins/data/hierarchy/attached_actions.html`

---

# Attached actions and context menus

A hierarchy item can expose dataset-specific operations by attaching `WidgetAction` objects. The hierarchy UI incorporates each attached action’s context menu.

```cpp
_exportAction.setToolTip("Export this dataset");

dataset->getDataHierarchyItem().addAction(_exportAction);
```

An attached action should describe behavior owned by your plugin or data implementation. `TriggerAction`, grouped actions, and settings actions can expose commands or controls without coupling the hierarchy UI to the implementing component.

`getActions()` returns the attached actions. `getContextMenu()` creates a menu containing their context menus, while `populateContextMenu(menu)` adds them to an existing menu. Actions configured with `WidgetAction::ConfigurationFlag::HiddenInActionContextMenu` are skipped.

## Ownership is not transferred

`addAction()` stores a non-owning pointer. The hierarchy item does not take QObject ownership and does not provide a public removal operation. Attach only an action guaranteed to outlive the hierarchy item.

This usually means:

- a dataset-owned action attached to that dataset’s item; or
- another action whose owner and teardown ordering guarantee that the dataset is removed first.

Attaching an ordinary plugin-instance member to a dataset that may outlive the plugin can leave a dangling pointer. When the lifetimes do not naturally align, expose the operation through plugin triggers or another discovery mechanism instead.

## Keep callbacks removal-safe

An action callback should retrieve or validate its target dataset when invoked:

```cpp
connect(&_exportAction, &QAction::triggered, this, [this]() {
    if (!_dataset.isValid())
        return;

    exportDataset(_dataset);
});
```

Disable or hide the action when the operation is unavailable, and detach plugin state during the dataset’s `aboutToBeRemoved` phase.
